#### Preface (9786267173633)

In a well-known chain café in Tokyo’s Ginza district, surrounded by the aroma of coffee, I pondered what to say and how to express it during the upcoming meeting. My thoughts were interrupted by the classic song “White Christmas” playing in the background. When I looked up, I saw the person I was scheduled to meet.

“Excuse me, are you Mr. Kojima?” I asked.

“Yes, I am Kojima. Are you Mr. Shimizu?” the man replied.

“Hello, I am Kenji Shimizu from the Institute of Facial Expression Science. Pleased to meet you!” I answered.

“Likewise, pleased to meet you.”

The man—Mr. Kojima—was a company president in his forties. His firm regularly organized lectures that applied psychology to improve business performance.

Information I had seen online sparked my interest in his business, and I hoped he would incorporate “micro-expressions” into the company’s lecture curriculum, so I arranged this meeting. That day, I explained to Mr. Kojima, whom I was meeting for the first time, that micro-expressions are useful not only in business but in all face-to-face communication. Mr. Kojima appeared engaged; his posture leaned slightly forward, palms facing me, as he listened attentively. However, when we began discussing a concrete business collaboration proposal, his smile lasted only an instant. In the next moment, one corner of his mouth lifted, and he began to speak.

Kojima: “Mr. Shimizu, you really do love micro-expressions! (At that moment, an asymmetric smile appeared on one side of his face.)”

I: “……Yes. I certainly do love micro-expressions.”

Kojima: “Sorry to interrupt. Please continue.”

I: “My apologies. I’ve been the only one speaking so far. May I ask for your opinion? Or shall we end the discussion here for today?”

Kojima: “Well…… Let’s leave it at that for now. I have a proposal regarding this matter. I suggest you return to university for further research and become Japan’s leading authority on micro-expressions before proceeding. I believe commercializing micro-expressions at this stage would be quite difficult. Perhaps we can revisit the idea once the timing is right. What do you think?”

After Mr. Kojima finished speaking, the atmosphere made it clear that no further progress would occur. He then stood up and left the café.

One month after the meeting, the expanding “Micro-expression Training Website” contacted me directly, at which point I learned that Mr. Kojima had appropriated my commercialization model. At the time, he had said, “Commercializing micro-expressions is very difficult,” yet his true intention had been to steal the model and develop it himself.

Do you know how I detected his inner thoughts? That’s right—it was from the micro-expression that flashed across his face for an instant.

In that moment during our conversation, an expression of “contempt” appeared!

“Contempt” is an attitude of superiority shown when comparing oneself with others. On the face, it appears as one corner of the mouth lifting. When I mentioned the business proposal, he displayed a dismissive attitude while simultaneously wanting to seize the business model. Fortunately, I noticed the micro-expression and, when discussing the core details of my model, hesitated and held back, so he did not obtain the critical information.

What I want to convey here is that, from both scientific and experiential perspectives, it is possible to discern another person’s true intentions. Therefore, I have studied various human thoughts and methods and compiled the discipline of “micro-expressions,” which allows one not only to see through others’ real intentions but also to avoid being disadvantaged in conversation.

“Micro-expressions” refer to unconscious facial expressions that last only 0.2 seconds. This aspect will be explained in detail later. Expressions are innate communication signals shared by all humans, regardless of culture, ethnicity, gender, age, or era; even people who are blind from birth display facial expressions.

If one can read these unconsciously displayed signs, it becomes possible to instantly interpret another person’s thoughts and emotions. Mastering the skill of reading micro-expressions, as mentioned earlier, further protects one from falling into traps. In recent years, communication methods that utilize facial expressions have gained increasing attention. In fact, many well-known companies with operations in Europe and the United States now provide micro-expression training.

In our daily lives, the ability to read expressions can be the key to gaining conversational initiative and control. The technique of reading micro-expressions is a science-based, entirely new communication technology.

Since becoming a business consultant specializing in micro-expression reading, I have met many people who are successful in their careers and fulfilled in their personal lives. In this book, I will introduce the “subtleties” of micro-expressions in a clear, practical manner that anyone can apply.

The skill of reading micro-expressions not only guides one toward professional success but also deepens understanding of human psychology and fosters better interpersonal relationships. I sincerely hope that every day you are surrounded by kind and positive emotions!

**Editor's Note**: The events described at the beginning of this book have been altered to a certain degree, without substantially changing the facts, so as not to point to specific individuals involved.

#### Preface (9787510438820)

Life is a masquerade; everyone hides their true expressions behind a mask. The person standing before you—is their speech sincere, or are they saying one thing while thinking another? Let an FBI special agent show you how to detect whether someone’s facial expressions are genuine or false, revealing their inner thoughts so clearly that pretense becomes impossible and concealment fails.

The FBI once arrested a spy. Although the spy was willing to discuss his own involvement in the case, he refused to name his accomplices. An experienced and seasoned FBI agent named Davidson used the following method. First, Davidson listed the names of everyone who had worked with the spy. He wrote each name on a small card and showed the cards to the spy one by one, asking him to describe each person briefly.

In reality, Davidson was not interested in the answers; he was watching the spy’s facial expressions. Although the spy maintained steady eye contact and gave negative answers, Davidson noticed that when the spy saw one particular name, his eyes suddenly widened, his pupils contracted rapidly, and he narrowed his eyes slightly.

Davidson, an expert in body language, knew that upon seeing his accomplice’s name the spy’s eyes had widened involuntarily from tension, yet he had quickly contracted his pupils to conceal his unease, resulting in a narrowed gaze. This was the information Davidson sought. He put the cards away and left.

The next day, Davidson showed the spy a photograph of the person whose name had triggered the reaction and said, “Tell me about this person.” The spy’s eyes widened like saucers. “How did you know?” he asked in surprise. Davidson replied, “You didn’t really think you were the only one cooperating with us, did you?” The spy cursed, “That bastard!” and then began to confess everything in detail. In the end, both spies were convicted.

So stop assuming that only a “second party,” “third party,” or “Nth party” can betray you. When your “little schemes” are guessed or your “hidden calculations” are seen through, it is often your micro-expressions that are to blame—in other words, your micro-expressions have given you away.

In fact, not only a glance or a frown, but every word and every movement conveys information and constitutes a bodily language. A person performs an action only when their body intends to do so.

I once attended a research meeting to discuss a new product of significant scientific value. The topics included patent rights, equity, royalties, research and development costs, and how to persuade the commissioning company to manufacture and sell the product.

At the start of the discussion, one member of the opposing team adopted an eager posture: sitting forward on the edge of the chair, body leaning in, toes touching the floor, like a sprinter waiting for the starting signal.

**Eager posture**

Because he was a technical specialist on their team, his reaction directly affected the outcome of my pitch. His “poised to act” posture told me he was interested in what we were discussing. I therefore guided him to raise technical questions, which our researchers answered one by one.

I had deliberately chosen to sit beside this key person from the outset so I could observe his every movement. Once we had fully addressed his technical concerns and removed his doubts, his attitude became highly cooperative.

The negotiation proceeded smoothly precisely because I immediately noticed the technical specialist’s posture indicating willingness to cooperate and made good use of that observation, allowing us to sign a mutually beneficial agreement quickly.

Gerard I. Nierenberg, known as the “father of negotiation training,” has shown through real negotiation experience that when communicating, simply paying a little attention to the other person’s micro-movements reveals their thoughts completely. No matter how casual a small movement may seem, it is triggered by psychological activity and fully exposes deeply buried mental states.

You may not know that micro-expressions are also called “facial micro-reactions,” and micro-movements are also called “bodily micro-reactions.” Together they form the broader term “micro-reactions” (微反应).

Whatever inner activity or emotional expression lies beneath a familiar or unfamiliar face can be seen at a glance through micro-reactions. Because micro-reactions are instantaneous, involuntary responses that occur the moment a person receives an effective stimulus—responses not controlled by conscious thought—they are instinctive reactions inherited through long-term biological evolution and cannot be deliberately “faked.” Therefore, they are the most accurate clues to a person’s true inner thoughts.

Micro-reactions act as an “amplifier” for reading inner emotions. Once this “amplifier” captures hidden “subtext” such as a twitching eyebrow, a nose rub, or crossed arms—like a scent-sensitive bloodhound—you will find that reading people is no longer difficult.

#### Preface (B07B3SW8DX)

You are enjoying a pleasant conversation with a friend when they suddenly fly into a rage. You are baffled, unsure why their mood changed so abruptly.

You visit a client, who sits with arms crossed. You feel puzzled, uncertain whether your presence is welcome.

You work diligently, yet your supervisor gives you no friendly looks and often criticizes you. Unable to read your supervisor’s emotional shifts, you can only endure again and again.

You quietly devote yourself at home, yet your family finds fault with you. You are at a loss, unsure how to please them.

……

In daily life, many people are skilled at disguising themselves and keeping their emotions from showing on their faces, which undoubtedly increases the difficulty of interacting with them. Therefore, it is necessary to learn some knowledge of micro-emotion psychology so that we can detect emotional fluctuations through others’ expressions, body movements, and words, thereby seeing through their psychology and piercing their disguises. Because emotions are neural responses to stimuli, they arise before rational thought, are uncontrollable physiological reactions, and cannot be deliberately faked. In other words, even the most skilled pretender cannot completely hide their emotions.

Your mind is often shrouded in the gloom of depression, feeling sorrow without reason.

Your temper is short; you are frequently provoked by others’ casual remarks and do not know how to extinguish the anger inside.

You often feel anxious and restless yet lack the strength to break free from this state.

You are constantly troubled by fear and long to overcome it but cannot find a way.

You cannot help suspecting others, doubting that people around you are plotting against you, even though you know you should not, yet you cannot control it.

……

Many people become trapped in negative emotions such as depression, anger, anxiety, fear, suspicion, and frustration, falling into the abyss of these feelings. In contrast, others consistently hold on to hope, embrace enthusiasm, remain confident, work actively, and maintain inner peace, as if living in a land of happiness. Why is this so? Faced with the same circumstances, why do people’s emotions differ so greatly? How do emotions arise? Is there a way to overcome them? These are major questions confronting every modern person.

As John Milton said, “He who can control his own emotions surpasses a king.” If we can control our emotions, release and resolve negative ones, and tap into latent positive ones, we hold the key to the door of happiness.

Identifying others’ emotions helps us interact with them better; decoding our own emotions helps us enjoy a happy life. This is the purpose of publishing this book and the value it offers. To achieve this goal, we adhere to the following basic principles:

1. Accessible language and strong readability  
   Most readers find specialized psychology works somewhat obscure, while overly superficial ones lack readability; both types discourage readers. This book presents micro-emotion psychology knowledge in accessible language while maintaining strong readability.

2. Comprehensive content with emphasis on practicality  
   Many books on micro-emotion psychology cover narrow topics and focus only on theory, offering little practical value. This book incorporates numerous research findings in micro-emotion psychology, spans a wide range of fields, and emphasizes solving real-world problems.

3. Simple methods with strong operability  
   This book introduces many straightforward techniques for controlling, expressing, and releasing emotions, drawing on professional therapies such as ACT, exposure therapy, dredging methods, color therapy, and art therapy. These methods are highly operable, and non-professionals can master them quickly.

#### Preface (9787510438820)

preface

A raised eyebrow or a lifted corner of the mouth reveals a person’s true thoughts! People’s faces write their inner secrets. Mastering certain decoding methods for facial expressions makes others’ pretense increasingly obvious and their concealment increasingly exposed.

Jack is a purchasing agent at a large manufacturing company. Because of his work, he frequently attends various business negotiations. Once, while discussing the purchase of components with a newly developed factory in another city, the other party quoted a price nearly 30 percent lower than competing bidders, with only one condition: Jack’s company must pay half the deposit in advance.

“I negotiated with their sales representative for over an hour. Throughout, he seemed very uneasy; his left hand kept making small movements—either pushing his glasses or rubbing his nose. While speaking, his eyes occasionally glanced upward to the right, and he frequently licked his lips. I suddenly recalled what Dr. Lightman said in Lie to Me: ‘Eyes looking left indicate recall; looking right indicates fabricating a lie.’ So I did not sign the contract immediately. Instead, I had an investigation agency check the other party’s credentials and discovered it was a shell company, saving my company nearly 500,000 yuan in losses.” Whenever Jack recounts this incident, he still becomes very emotional.

Eye movements and raised eyebrows—do not underestimate these micro-expressions; they may be the crucial signals that allow you to see through the other person and turn the situation around. As the French writer Diderot said, “Every movement of a person’s mind is displayed on their face, clearly and distinctly drawn.”

You have an interview for a new job and are eager to try, yet the competition is strong. You feel very nervous and hope to make a good impression on the interviewer. What can you do?

From the moment you meet the interviewer, you must pay attention to your own body language: smile and look directly at the person. If they smile back, you have made a good start. If their face remains expressionless, do not let your anxiety show. Maintain eye contact and respond positively to the interviewer’s body language to break through their defenses: if they keep a tense face, you smile; if their posture is stiff, you relax—as if mirroring them.

Remember not to cross your arms or cross your legs; keep your feet roughly parallel and sit facing the interviewer. Let your hands rest loosely at your sides or on your knees, and keep your eyes level—do not glance around. Leaning slightly forward can convey a positive impression, but do not lean too close, as that may feel oppressive. If you notice the interviewer unconsciously leaning back, try relaxing your posture and leaning back slightly.

Life is a game, and living is a contest. If you can accurately read others’ micro-expressions and also make good use of your own—avoiding or minimizing negative expressions and movements—you will navigate social and business interactions with ease and ultimately achieve happiness and success in life.

#### Preface (9787538583373)

Whenever we see an unfamiliar face, we unconsciously make basic judgments: Is the face round or long? Are the eyes large or small? Are the lips thick or thin? Is the makeup neat? Is the smile friendly? The purpose is to judge the person’s basic character from their expression and decide whether we like them. Unfortunately, the expressions we see are not always genuine, which directly affects our initial judgment. Therefore, judging micro-expressions becomes extremely important.

The shortest duration of a micro-expression is 1/25 of a second, and the longest does not exceed 1/4 of a second. Because the time is so brief, it is extremely easy to overlook. Yet these fleeting expressions betray many deliberately concealed true emotions.

Through the study of micro-expressions, we learn that a smile does not always indicate happiness—it can also signify sarcasm, helplessness, or contempt. Crying does not always indicate sadness—it can also signify fear or joy. A furrowed brow is not always anger—it can also indicate thinking or worry. A pout is not always disdain—it can also indicate sadness or suppressed laughter.

Learning and studying micro-expressions helps us make more accurate judgments and reduces unnecessary difficulties and obstacles in interpersonal relationships. It must be noted, however, that micro-expression research cannot be completed through a single book; it requires long-term training and observation. Moreover, micro-expressions are not meant for pranks, showing off, or harming others. Therefore, before learning about micro-expressions, please prepare a kind intention.

#### The "Tricks" of Success

In many people’s eyes, I was once a successful actor and am now a successful professional analyst; perhaps in the future I will pursue yet another field. At every stage of life I ask myself: Have you truly recognized yourself? Have you truly recognized this job? Have you truly recognized the people around you? These three questions are as simple as can be, yet few people ever truly think them through. Let us now discuss these three questions.

Socrates said: “Know thyself.”

Money, material goods, or power are not necessary conditions here. The first step toward success is to recognize yourself and your work. I have what I have today because I have always known what I want to do, what I am suited to do, and how to put it into practice. A person who does not even know their own character or abilities is like a headless fly, bumping into walls until it is battered and bleeding.

King Solomon said: “With all you possess, obtain understanding.”

Once I have a clear understanding of myself and my work, I draw on all my experience and reason to “understand” the attitudes of those around me, including family members, the personalities of colleagues, the psychology of clients, and how to build good interactions with them. Whether a person succeeds depends largely on their ability to get along harmoniously with the people around them.

If you have studied the great or successful figures of history, you will find that they each possess at least one of the following two traits:

- First, they identified a life goal aligned with their interests and talents and pursued it with determination.
- Second, they possessed a keen eye for people and excelled at evaluating others.

These are the “tricks” of success I mentioned at the outset. This book will teach you the basic principles and operating methods of these “tricks.”

Of course, mastering the “tricks” of recognizing yourself and recognizing others is no easy matter, because humans are highly skilled at deception and disguise. We say things we do not mean and do things we do not want to do; when happy we can pretend to be sad, and when in pain we deliberately appear calm. Sometimes we cannot even figure out what we ourselves are thinking, let alone what others are thinking!

Fortunately, when God created humanity, a unique “clue” was left on each person’s body. Master these “clues,” follow them, and you can see into a person’s inner world, perceive the real them, and everything else will follow naturally.

Many years ago, a craftsman brought his fourteen-year-old son to my office. “Mr. Balken,” he said, “I would like you to analyze whether this boy is suited to carpentry. His hands are very dexterous; sometimes he spends the whole day whittling and is completely absorbed. I am wondering whether he should quit school and begin learning woodworking with me now. I believe he will become an excellent carpenter earning eight dollars a day.”

I looked at the boy seriously, exchanged a few words with him, then told the father: “Yes, this child is very caring—not only toward wood but toward the whole world. If I am not mistaken, he must enjoy helping others. For such a compassionate and dexterous child to quit school and become a carpenter earning eight dollars a day would be a waste of talent. My suggestion is to send him to medical school to specialize in surgery, so he can help others while fully realizing his own value. Trust me, he will be happy—and he will earn far more than eight dollars a day.”

The kindhearted carpenter father followed my advice. The boy did not disappoint; he graduated with honors from medical school and is now a distinguished surgeon.

My recommendation that the boy study surgery was based on the key knowledge in this book—grasping the “clues” God left on his body. Through these subtle “clues,” I saw in him something far more precious than mere mechanical talent.

For many readers this may still seem abstract. To be specific, a person’s appearance, voice, and manner are intricately linked to their inner world.

During my acting career I met all kinds of people every day (and even more so now). One of my interests has been to infer character traits, occupation, family situation, current mood, and whether someone is lying simply by observing their outward expressions. I have found that the more educated, accomplished, or high-status the person, the more interesting the exchange, because they, like me, are constantly reading subtle expressions. If I do not take the initiative, I risk being found out—you know, even with all my experience reading people, I cannot completely control my own micro-expressions.

Expressions—static expressions (such as body type, skin color, bone structure) and dynamic expressions (facial expressions, voice, movements of the hands and feet)—together form a complete system. The amount of information it contains is vast and complex, yet the system is simple to operate and highly effective. In the chapters that follow, I will concretize this seemingly complex system so that you can master this “technique” in the shortest possible time and take the shortcut to success and happiness.

#### Preface: "Listening" with Your Eyes

By observing details such as a person’s fingernails, shirt collar and cuffs, shoes, the knee areas of trousers, calluses on the index finger and thumb, and manner of speech and behavior, one can clearly determine a person’s occupation.

—Arthur Conan Doyle

The observation of surrounding things has proven to be an extremely attractive pastime. In public places such as shopping centers, grocery stores, conference rooms, social gatherings, or sporting events, we all occasionally observe others. If you are like us, you will find yourself guessing others’ psychology: Why did they behave this way or make that decision?

For example, when someone sticks out their tongue, makes a face, or tilts their head, it indicates a specific thought or emotion. Whether or not they speak, the information conveyed by their body movements fully reflects their thoughts and feelings. Even when they do speak, in most cases we should simultaneously pay attention to the information conveyed by their body language to confirm whether what they said is true.

Being aware of the emotions and intentions behind people’s behavior is very helpful in life. By practicing the methods provided in this book repeatedly, you can clearly grasp what triggers these behaviors. With this deeper understanding, you will be able to handle all kinds of interpersonal relationships in a highly professional, relaxed, and efficient manner.

By reading this book you will learn how to train yourself to observe the nonverbal information around you more carefully. You will begin to learn to “listen” with your eyes and carefully consider the meanings conveyed by people’s gestures or expressions<|eos|>

#### Talking and Laughing, But No Deal in the End—Why?

May I ask, in work or daily-life communication situations, have you ever experienced the following—

- In a business setting, the discussion was lively, yet no deal was closed?
- Responding as usual to a client’s casual inquiry, only for it to turn into a complaint incident!
- Your supervisor listened to your presentation with a smile, yet did not adopt your proposal?
- The contract was signed, but did you concede too much?
- Fooled! The investment pitch that “guarantees profits” was all lies!
- A subordinate who was “in excellent shape” suddenly developed emotional issues…
- A couple who reconciled after an argument suddenly says they want to break up?

How do you feel about the situations listed above? Do they resonate strongly? The common thread hidden in all of them is “failing to read the other person’s true intention.”

Eh? Is this an obvious matter? Of course, if you could understand the other person’s true intention, the communication scenes mentioned earlier would not produce misunderstandings. To prevent misunderstandings, how can you correctly grasp the other person’s true intention and achieve good communication?

This is the key point this book explains; the secret is to read the other person’s “micro-expressions (微表情).”

Let me give an example and think backward. Imagine the kind of person who can easily solve the problems above, or skillfully avert crises before they occur, and communicate smoothly with all kinds of people. Do you have such a person around you—

- The top-performing salesperson, the insurance broker with a high closing rate;
- The service staff requested by many clients;
- The colleague who gives excellent presentations;
- The interviewer who accurately judges candidates;
- The supervisor followed by many subordinates;
- The first-rate manager who revives multiple companies;
- The businessperson whose life runs smoothly.

Why does the person who comes to mind not seem ordinary?

What timing, what circumstances, and how do these people who are good at communication choose what to say and what attitude to adopt with the other party? How do they do it? Similar questions inevitably arise, don’t they? These people understand “reading the room” and “seeing into people’s hearts.” Yet even when we know that “reading the room” and “seeing into people’s hearts” are important, most people still do not know what to do.

In fact, even if you ask “Why are you so good at reading the room?” “How can you correctly know what others really mean?” or “How are you so good at communicating?”, the usual answers are “I don’t know” or “It’s just a natural reaction.”

Even if you accept that “one day I will naturally possess communication ability,” reality is urgent; because insight is usually reflected directly in work results, to survive in the workplace you must acquire this ability as early as possible.

#### Reading the Room Is a Powerful Communication Tool

The “reading the room” and “seeing into people’s hearts” mentioned in the previous section play a very important role in communication. How exactly should one observe, and how should one perceive? Most people do not understand, and therefore many may not even know whether their own communication methods are correct or incorrect; they keep repeating the same mistakes, thinking they can learn from erroneous experiences, yet they cannot come up with better solutions.

You may want to ask others how to achieve “reading the room” and “seeing into people’s hearts,” but most people who possess this ability may not clearly know why they can sense the atmosphere of an interaction and can only explain it as a rule of thumb gained through long-term observation and correction.

The rules of thumb developed through experience are sometimes correct and sometimes incorrect. Moreover, such rules of thumb are useful only for certain people and offer limited help to most.

The current situation is that those who learn rules of thumb from communication experts do not know how to learn them correctly, and the teachers themselves do not know how to teach them correctly. The main reason is that the abilities of “reading the room” and “seeing into people’s hearts” have not yet been technologized—that is, they have not been systematically organized. Even if one is a communication expert, everyone’s situations and environments differ, so it is not easy to convey the skill universally.

In conclusion, possessing the ability to read “micro-expressions” is equivalent to having a powerful communication tool that can be easily applied in daily life or work.

In other words, by understanding the other person’s expressions, you perceive their true intention and communicate smoothly.

In fact, various studies show a direct connection between the ability to read micro-expressions and communication skills. For example, top-performing salespeople, interviewers who accurately judge whether candidates are lying, and management consultants who revive multiple companies cannot clearly explain to others how strong their communication ability is, but they share the common trait of possessing excellent micro-expression reading ability.

There is no doubt that people who are good at “reading the room” and “seeing into people’s hearts” are actually the ones who instantly see through the other person’s micro-expressions and immediately perceive and interpret their meaning.

Because micro-expressions are scientific, both the generation of expressions and how to train the ability to read micro-expressions can be explained systematically. The science of micro-expressions turns these communication experts’ rules of thumb into something “visualizable,” converting rules of thumb into a technology. Once technologized, it becomes easier to learn communication skills and correctly perceive and interpret micro-expressions.

Scientific research shows that in daily communication, 7% of information is conveyed through words, 38% through voice, and 55% through facial expressions and body posture.

Words can lie, but the body cannot. Even if you are silver-tongued, your body will betray you and clearly reveal your true inner thoughts to others. Likewise, you can observe and interpret others’ micro-expressions to see into their hearts. In other words, personality analysis is a two-way process.

Psychology master William James once said: “The main cause of all emotions originates from the physical.”

The human mind and body are closely connected; even the slightest physical influence moves the mind. Scientific personality analysis is built on this connection between physiology and psychology. Any emotional expression—joy, happiness, sorrow, anger, melancholy, fear, and so on—reaches the muscles, blood, and other bodily components, triggering a series of external manifestations. The more often you repeat the same emotion, the deeper the “imprint” left on the body; over time, these seemingly insignificant “imprints” become the “display” of inner emotions.
