#### Eye Shape Interpretation

##### 22. Uneven Eyes

People with uneven eyes are very cunning in their dealings. They are usually quite talented, have deep scheming, are good at strategizing, and handle matters with superb skill. This type of person has a volatile temperament and often experiences self-contradictory situations; their inner self is both inferior and stubborn; their emotional life or career tends to fluctuate and waver, but their financial luck is quite good. If a woman has uneven eyes, she is both talented and competitive, can make a good impression on the surface, can easily control and dominate others, and is also extremely skilled at hiding her shortcomings. However, people with uneven eyes are more likely to remarry. Generally speaking, if a man's left eye is larger, he is prone to discord with his father and wife, and has a tendency toward male chauvinism; if the right eye is larger, he will have no affinity with his mother, and may be afraid of his wife, and may also be more affectionate toward women other than his wife. If a woman has a larger left eye and smaller right eye, she is very likely to fear her husband and will work tirelessly for him. Overall, having the left eye larger than the right is relatively better, with better financial prospects, and those who fear their wives are more likely to gain a virtuous helper.

##### c. Myopic Squinting Eyes

The cause of nearsightedness is that when viewing near objects for long periods, the lens remains in a tense deformed state under the action of the ciliary muscle and has difficulty returning to normal. As a result, distant objects cannot form an image on the retina, creating nearsightedness.

Squinting the eyes forcefully allows the orbicularis oculi muscle to slightly alter the front-to-back circumference of the eyeball through compression, thereby mildly improving image quality. Therefore, nearsighted students who do not wear glasses will squint when they need to see something clearly, which helps to some degree. However, once the structure of the eyeball and the principles of image formation are understood, it becomes clear that only by engaging the ciliary muscle to flatten the lens can image quality truly be changed. Since the ciliary muscle is controlled by the autonomic nervous system and cannot be moved at will, squinting to compensate for nearsightedness is of limited help.

##### 9. Double Eyelids: Warm and Outgoing

People with double eyelids have an open and generous personality, and are candid and enthusiastic. Their minds are flexible and they adapt quickly. Although their eyes look attractive, they lack perseverance and patience in their work, are highly emotional, and tend to act on feelings. Double eyelids are classified by whether the eyelid is long or round. Those with long eyelids belong to the emotionally rich yet fragile type. They have poor resilience and resistance to setbacks, and lack perseverance and constancy. Those with round eyelids (where the central part of the eyelid curves upward into a rounder shape) have an open, innocent, and lively personality, but are also easily deceived and must therefore exercise extra caution. In addition, there is a rarer case of one single eyelid and one double eyelid. Such people tend to be rather contrary. For example, after deciding on something and having it approved by others, they may ultimately reject it themselves, showing a tendency toward self-contradiction and indecision.

##### 24. Drooping Eye Corners

People with drooping eye corners are strongly influenced by their childhood experiences and early education. If they receive a good education from a young age and develop noble character, they are more likely to become successful members of society. In social interactions, they usually benefit, often receiving help from others and support from benefactors, giving them a high chance of success. However, if their childhood was unhappy, they may develop a rebellious mindset. They become wary of others and do not trust people easily. If they enter business under these circumstances, they may act unscrupulously and to the detriment of others for personal gain. If a girl is born with drooping eye corners, her personality will be gentle and endearing; she will be affectionate, family-oriented, and a classic virtuous wife and mother.

##### 8. Single Eyelids: Opinionated and Strong-Willed

People with single eyelids are proactive, calm, and possess strong willpower. They have firm opinions, good judgment, and can endure hardship and setbacks. Most are introverted, highly self-respecting, somewhat suspicious, and occasionally display a timid side. In handling interpersonal matters, their excessive competitiveness and strong self-awareness can lead to disagreements and strained relationships. Girls with single eyelids tend to be shy and yearn for a steady, long-lasting relationship, so persistence is required when pursuing them.

##### 10. Multiple Eyelids: Emotionally Rich

Multiple layers of eyelids indicate that a person is emotionally rich. As their friend, one is sure to be valued by them and can form a deep, lasting bond. Even with acquaintances, they remain warm and likable. Their shortcoming is that they are sensitive and impulsive, often overthinking when they see others talking behind their backs, and may even join in to offer their own opinions. If the eyelids are of the inner double type, emotional and rational sides are balanced, making this the best eyelid form and indicating a friend worth knowing well.

##### 1. Eyes Wide Open

If a person's eyes are wider than usual, with raised eyebrows and furrowed brow, it indicates anger. When someone stares directly at another person with tense eye muscles and tightly squinted eyelids, it shows intense anger. This action is meant to vent inner rage and to intimidate or threaten the other party. Additionally, if a person's eyes are wide open, mouth agape, and expression rigid, it generally signifies extreme fear or shock.

##### 19. Peach Blossom Eyes

This type of eye is always full of smiles, with the center of the lower eyelid curving upward in a crescent shape. The eyes appear bright and moist, conveying a captivating gaze. People with peach blossom eyes are romantic by nature, enjoy excellent opposite-sex relationships, and lead colorful emotional lives, yet they may also attract trouble. Women with peach blossom eyes tend to be easygoing and approachable, with little defensiveness. Their social skills are not strong, they find it hard to refuse others, and they are easily swayed by temptation.

##### 20. Triangular Eyes

As the name suggests, the eyes resemble triangles. Such people may appear fierce and give off a coercive impression. In fact, they are often cunning, competitive, aggressive, and unwilling to admit defeat; they may also be stubborn and hold extreme views. When a man has this eye shape, he may become a formidable figure like Cao Cao. A woman with this eye shape may dominate her husband after marriage.

##### 12. Narrow Eye Spacing

People whose eyes are close together act decisively and efficiently. They also have good eyesight and accurate vision. However, they tend to be introverted, narrow-minded, impatient, and often gloomy or overly anxious. Although their gaze is sharp, it lacks long-term vision; they focus on immediate gains. They are prone to suspicion and jealousy, are calculating, lack persistence, and are changeable.

##### 13. Wide Eye Spacing

Generally, the ideal spacing between the eyes equals the length of one eye. People with wider spacing have a broader field of vision, are open-minded and mild-mannered, and tend to encounter more opportunities than others. They are tolerant, handle relationships well, and are well-liked. It should be noted that if the spacing is excessively wide, the person may be overly timid, hesitant, and inactive.

##### 7. Many Worries

People who harbor many worries show numerous wrinkles at the outer corners of the eyes. They carry too many troubles and experience ups and downs in their emotional lives. Because they overthink, they may appear somewhat neurotic. They are also vain, self-centered, have weak self-control, weak ethical standards, and lack a sense of responsibility.

##### 17. Knife-Cut Outer Eye Corners

Such people are talented in both civil and military affairs, emotionally refined, conscientious, quick-witted, insightful into human nature, and magnanimous and refined in character, handling matters comprehensively. A woman with this eye shape makes a capable and supportive partner. People whose inner eye corners are sharply hooked like a bird's beak have good memory and can handle many different types of work.

##### 21. Deep-Set Heavy Eyes

Small or deeply recessed eyes are called heavy eyes. Most people with heavy eyes inherit the trait. Small eyes indicate a narrow field of vision, so the personality tends to be stubborn, selfish, conservative, and suspicious. Yet they are also tenacious, unwilling to give up or admit defeat, and possess perseverance, which can bring them certain rewards.

##### 18. Watery Eyes

Eyes that appear moist and glistening are very appealing, especially in girls. Such people have richer emotional lives than their peers and may occasionally act in ways that seem inconsistent with their appearance. Because their looks are endearing, they form particularly good connections with the opposite sex.

##### 23. Upward-Tilted Eye Corners

These individuals have strong persistence. Once they set a goal, they move forward resolutely, remain undisturbed by external factors, stay calm, and hold firm beliefs. In girls, this trait may lead to indecision in love; due to insecurity, they easily develop jealousy, which can cause relationships to end.

#### Basic Emotions in the Eyes

##### 3. Eyes Lighting Up

Usually, when a person is happy, especially surprised, the phenomenon of “eyes lighting up” appears. The cause of this phenomenon is not an illusion; the eyes truly become “brighter.”

When surprised, the eyes widen, exposing a larger area of both the iris and the sclera (the white of the eye). On one hand, the overall reflective surface increases; on the other, positive stimuli cause pupil dilation, and combined with the pigmented iris, the contrast between this darker region and the lighter sclera becomes more pronounced, making the eyes appear brighter. In addition, the increased blood circulation from excitement does, to some extent, add energy to the eyes, which also contributes positively to their brightness.

Conversely, most sad eyes (assuming no grief or indignation) give the impression of a dull gaze. This is essentially the reverse of the above: the exposed area of the eyeball decreases due to eyelid closure, the contrast between light and dark regions weakens, and without the micro-circulatory changes brought by excitement, the eyes naturally appear lifeless.

##### 4. The Gaze of Fear

When facing a fear stimulus, people often exhibit a distinctive eye movement—rapid, multi-directional shifts of the eyeballs.

This action is difficult to fake; it is not impossible, but hard to perform convincingly. Only the alertness triggered by fear prompts the high-frequency eye movements that allow quick attention to every change in the surroundings—an evolved instinct.

The value of this stress micro-expression lies in the fact that the frequency of changes in gaze direction is directly proportional to the degree of inner fear.

### Nose

#### II. Psychological Signals from the Nose

People’s understanding of the nose often centers on its role in breathing. Many have experienced the urge to sneeze in an environment with an unusual or strong scent, at which point the sensitive nose responds with corresponding expansion and contraction.

The nose, in its shape, relates to a person’s temperament. As one of the five sensory organs, it is the least mobile part of the face. Although its expressions are fewer than those of the eyes or other organs, the nose possesses its own distinct language with very clear meanings. Therefore, people can discern another’s inner thoughts from the subtle language of the nose.

In daily life, we can “observe the heart through the nose.” Minor changes in the nose may reveal your true inner thoughts. If you observe those around you, you will notice that some people’s noses sweat easily, perhaps indicating they are in a tense or constrained environment—this is a sign of psychological agitation. Others may suddenly see their noses turn pale, reflecting a very negative emotional state manifesting physiologically in the nose. In addition, when people are angry, their nostrils flare outward involuntarily, signaling that they are forcefully suppressing negative emotions.

Even a small nose can reveal many bodily secrets during conversation.

1. **Wrinkling the nose**: The person finds your conversation or behavior distasteful  
   When someone violates traffic rules, spits on the ground, encounters an irritating odor, or hears statements they disagree with, people often make a “sniffing” expression. The nose twitches slightly upward with obvious expansion and contraction. These subtle changes represent the nose owner’s psychological reaction of venting inner dissatisfaction or disgust, and these inner activities are openly betrayed by the nose’s movements.

2. **Flaring nostrils**: The person is angry and experiencing dissatisfaction  
   The Chinese idiom “seven orifices emitting smoke” describes extreme anger. When angry, a person’s nostrils generally flare outward. During anger or while forcefully suppressing inner emotions, people breathe more air to relieve inner agitation, causing the nostrils to expand with small but noticeable opening and closing movements. If you misspeak during a conversation, watch whether the other person’s nose shows these signs and remedy your mistake promptly.

3. **Sweating nose**: The person is in a state of tension or agitation  
   Generally, if someone whose nose does not normally sweat easily suddenly begins to sweat, it indicates that their environment is making them feel tense or agitated, with psychological emotions subtly manifesting on the nose. When facing sudden changes or problems that must be solved, people become involuntarily tense, and the tip of the nose begins to sweat. Sometimes this physiological sign appears when people try to hide inner anxiety or cover up a mistake.

4. **Change in nose color**: The person’s mood is negative and they are in a withdrawn state  
   Many ask whether the nose can change color. In normal circumstances, the nose does not change color unless a health issue arises or inner emotions fluctuate significantly. A sudden paling of the nose indicates the person has suffered a major blow, had their self-esteem wounded, or feels guilt. Reddening of the nose warrants attention to personal health, as long-term alcohol consumption, excessive spicy food, endocrine disorders, cardiovascular disease, or abnormal liver function can cause the nose to redden or darken.

5. **Touching the nose**: The person is concealing the truth and feels resistance or hesitation  
   Many have seen the American drama *Lie to Me*, in which Dr. Cal Lightman solves a complex criminal case by reading the micro-expression of nose-touching. Psychology holds that touching the nose is a very subtle action that reveals much about inner psychological activity. First, if you ask someone for help during a conversation and they unconsciously touch their nose, you can infer they feel resistance to your request, even if they verbally agree. Second, if the other person keeps touching their nose while you discuss a topic, it basically shows they are not interested, and you should tactfully switch to a more engaging subject. Finally, when facing temporarily unsolvable problems, people may unconsciously touch their noses to give themselves psychological comfort or to hide their true thoughts.

   Note that touching the bridge of the nose indicates deep thought and inner struggle, not necessarily concealment. These subtle differences can lead to different interpretations of the information revealed.

#### Never Scratch Your Nose When Lying

Have you ever felt an itch in your nose while lying and unconsciously touched it to relieve the discomfort? Remember the protagonist Pinocchio in the classic Italian fairy tale *The Adventures of Pinocchio*? Whenever he lied, his nose grew longer.

Several American scientists recently discovered that the saying “lying makes the nose grow” is not groundless. They explain that when a person lies, anxiety increases blood flow to the nose, causing slight swelling. Although this change may not be obvious and others might not notice it with the naked eye, the liar feels an itch from the nasal tissue congestion and scratches it.

The scientists even studied Bill Clinton’s testimony to the grand jury regarding the Monica Lewinsky affair. They found that Clinton rarely touched his nose when telling the truth, but whenever he lied, his brow would furrow slightly before the lie, and he touched his nose once every four minutes, totaling 26 touches during the testimony.

Drawing on accumulated experience and extensive field practice, FBI agents also consider touching or lightly rubbing the nose (usually with the index finger) a typical lying expression.

Many years ago, the late renowned body-language expert Professor Ray L. Birdwhistell discussed a book he had written with a young man. When the professor asked the young man’s opinion of the book, the young man rubbed his nose and said he liked it very much.

Professor Birdwhistell smiled and said, “You’re lying. You don’t like the book at all.” The young man was stunned, but he did not understand how he had given himself away and had to admit he had only read a few pages before finding the writing “really dull.”

It was unfortunate for the young man that he rubbed his nose in front of a body-language expert.

Nose-touching is a common gesture, but does every instance mean the speaker is lying? Jiang Zhenyu, head of the China University of Political Science and Law micro-reaction research group and lecturer of the “Psychological Stress Micro-reaction” course, answered on the program *Extraordinary Knowledge*: “When reading people through micro-expressions, one must also consider whether this is a momentary unconscious reaction and not rigidly apply micro-expression dogma. Some people habitually touch their noses; this cannot be judged as lying.” Moreover, directly interpreting nose-touching while speaking as “wanting to hide something” would be unfair to those with rhinitis!

Therefore, we should not interpret every gesture so absolutely. Determining whether someone is lying requires combining other lying indicators. Sometimes the other person touches their nose simply because of pollen allergy, a cold, or discomfort from glasses pressing on it.

However, there remains a clear difference between rubbing the nose due to discomfort and touching it due to lying. Rubbing due to discomfort is forceful, while touching due to lying is very gentle—usually a quick rub along the lower edge of the nose with the hand, sometimes just a light touch that is almost imperceptible. The latter action also appears elegant and is often accompanied by other gestures such as crossed arms, fidgeting, or rapid blinking.

“In fact, when we see the nose-touching gesture, if we can confirm the other person has no nasal discomfort, we can work backward to conclude that the person is excited (or nervous). The key is to analyze why this physiological change occurred. What caused the excitement (or tension)? Was it the question you asked, the answer they gave, something that happened earlier, or a situation that might occur later? Combining these contextual factors and ruling out purely physiological causes such as illness may reveal what the nose-toucher is nervous about,” Dr. Jiang Zhenyu further explained.

In any case, we must remind you: next time you lie, never scratch your nose!

#### Section 1: The Most Temperamental Nose

A Chinese saying states that “appearance is born from the heart,” meaning a person’s temperament can be seen in their facial features. Many begin observing a person from their appearance, and people usually look at the eyes first because a pair of clear, bright eyes do not lie; one can observe character and temperament from the gaze. In truth, the nose, like the eyes, can reveal personality and temperament, yet people often overlook observing the nose.

In ancient times, many scholars and Taoists predicted people’s futures through facial reading or divination, including a so-called “nose-reading technique.” It was said that one could understand a person’s character, temperament, and fate from the length, width, tilt, and protrusion of the nose, giving rise to the saying “the nose gathers wealth.” These ancient nose-reading techniques may seem mysterious and unscientific to modern people. However, the nose, located at the center of the face and one of the five sensory organs, allows us to scientifically observe its changes and discern temperament and psychological activity from its subtle shifts.

Physiologically, the nose is one of the respiratory passages. In Roy Hess’s *Human Aesthetics*, it is noted: “Since Aristotle, people have believed that the nose is closely related to character, and it is the earliest organ to form in the human embryo, also regarded as a symbol of beauty.” Thus, the nose plays a vital role in facial features.

“Sniffing” describes disdain or contempt for certain people or matters, while “nostrils pointing to the sky” describes arrogant individuals. Therefore, the nose is indeed closely linked to inner emotions. In daily life, we can observe inner emotional fluctuations and psychological activity through breathing-induced changes in the nose’s shape and color, because inadvertent nasal changes often most fully and truthfully reflect what people are thinking.

In the animal kingdom, animals without language maintain contact and communication within their groups through various actions, including using the nose to express inner emotions. Biological research reports indicate that animals habitually bare their teeth to show anger and signal an attack. At the same time, an angry animal’s nostrils flare to allow the lungs to take in more oxygen, enabling them to enter a tense fight-or-flight state. When animals are angry, their nostrils flare; humans, when expressing anger, also exhibit this alongside language or body movements. In addition, people’s casual nose movements reveal different emotional changes. Understanding the information conveyed by the nose is increasingly important for social interaction in daily life. To gain an advantage in social situations, one must know both oneself and others by fully understanding the emotions hidden deep within.

The nose is a window into a person’s temperament. Generally, a person with a peaceful mind shows no change in the nose. If the other person’s nose slightly expands during conversation, it indicates inner feelings of pride, anger, or fear—perhaps they are restraining or suppressing their true emotions. If the other person touches their nose from time to time while talking with you, you should consider whether they are concealing the truth or disagreeing with what you said. This is a compulsive action that is generally difficult to hide. Research shows that when lying, psychological suggestion increases blood flow to the nose, causing it to swell and itch. In addition, when nervous, the nose may sweat unconsciously or change color. These subtle nasal changes can help people understand the other person’s true psychological state.

Thus, like the other sensory organs, the nose has its own unique expressive language, and these subtle expressions reveal bodily and psychological secrets.

#### How the Nose Expresses Emotions

Alfred recently wrote me a letter saying: “…I applied the people-reading techniques you taught me to sales, and my performance has been excellent lately—even my boss finds it unbelievable. Thank you so much! I now find work truly enjoyable.” His performance, once average, has now risen to second in the entire company. This once again gave me and my theory.

The above is merely a brief interlude before entering the theme of this section. What I want to discuss next is the nose. Yes, this part that you may have overlooked can also convey a great deal of silent information.

Have you ever noticed the noses of Africans? Most are short and flat with wide nostrils; I call this the “concave-type nose.” People from cold regions are the opposite: Anglo-Saxon noses are usually long, allowing thin cold air to warm slightly in the nasal cavity before entering the lungs. Therefore, nasal features are closely related to lung function. Generally, people with strong lung function have larger noses. These individuals often have well-developed motor skills, lively personalities, decisive actions, and strong ambition. Being with them, you feel full of sunshine and vitality. Conversely, people with weak lung function have smaller nostrils, lack ambition, dabble in everything without depth, and most are lazy.

To help you better understand the secrets of the nose, I have specially prepared the following table for your reference.

| Name | Physical Features | Personality and Psychological Traits |
|------|-------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Small nose | Short nasal bridge, small nostrils | Cheerful personality; insufficient willpower, easily influenced; most are relatively lazy and lack the courage to change their lives |
| Greek nose | Long, straight nasal bridge forming a sloping straight line, high nose shape | High taste, good understanding of art, pursuit of beauty and nobility; very confident but prone to pride, giving an impression of being difficult to approach; some prefer solitude |
| Depressed nose | Nasal bridge not straight but concave | Cheerful personality, can be close even with strangers |
| Straight nose | Nasal bridge straight, nose shape lower than Greek nose | Relatively selfish, pays attention to details; rational, smoother at work; popular with the opposite sex but also easily abandoned |
| Aquiline nose | Shaped like an eagle’s beak, tip hooked downward | Cold and fierce personality, very greedy |
| Broken nose | Nasal bridge shows a break in the middle | Quite stubborn, difficult to compromise; strong aggression in personality, easily offends others |
| Fleshy nose | Thick flesh | Obsessed with money, willing to endure curses, typical miser; smooth in dealings, flexible in social interactions |

The nose undergoes certain changes in specific situations. For example, when stimulated by an odor, the nostrils expand noticeably and the entire nose may tremble slightly. From a medical perspective, when a person is excited or tense, breathing and heartbeat accelerate, causing nostril expansion. Therefore, if the other person’s nose enlarges during conversation, there are usually three possibilities: pride, dissatisfaction, or suppression of emotion. Additionally, a sweating nose tip indicates inner anxiety or tension, so the side with a sweating nose tip during negotiations often loses. Wrinkling the nose indicates disgust; “humming” through the nose indicates disdain and rejection; trembling the nose indicates tension. Another interesting phenomenon is that when a person experiences negative emotions such as fear, apprehension, embarrassment, or unease, the nose turns pale.

Thus, although the nose is the least dynamic facial organ, it still hints at much information. Combining nasal characteristics with those of other parts helps you more accurately detect the other person’s inner thoughts.

#### Touching the Nose May Indicate Lying

When a person lies, even if they try their hardest to conceal it, some flaws will always show. For example, when someone frequently touches their nose, they are likely lying.

"My dear child, lies are easy to spot because there are only two kinds: one with short legs and one with a long nose. The lie you told has a long nose." These are words from the famous fairy tale *Pinocchio*. In the world of this tale, whenever the protagonist Pinocchio lies, his nose grows longer.

Scientists at the Smell & Taste Treatment and Research Foundation in Chicago, USA, discovered that when people lie, they release a chemical substance called catecholamine, which causes the cells inside the nasal cavity to swell. Using special imaging equipment that displays blood flow inside the body, the scientists also revealed that during lying, a person's nose enlarges due to increased blood flow, raising the internal temperature of the nasal cavity. This causes the nose to swell and produce an itchy sensation, so people can only frequently rub their noses with their hands to relieve the itch. Therefore, touching the nose is a relatively common body movement when a person lies.

When lying, the insular cortex of the brain, which regulates body temperature, is activated; this is the main mechanism behind the rise in nose-tip temperature. The cerebral hemispheres are divided into five lobes: frontal, parietal, occipital, temporal, and insular. The insular lobe is triangular and island-shaped, located deep in the lateral sulcus and covered by the frontal, parietal, occipital, and temporal lobes. It is closely related to the brain's reward mechanism, helping convert a person's desires for other things into "actions that achieve satisfaction." The insula becomes active when a person experiences real feelings. When someone exerts every effort to psychologically suggest to themselves that they are not lying, their nose-tip temperature gradually returns to normal levels.

American psychiatrist Charles Wolf and neurologist Alan Hirsch conducted an in-depth study of Bill Clinton's testimony to the jury regarding the Monica Lewinsky scandal. They were surprised to find that Clinton generally did not touch his nose when telling the truth. However, every time he lied, before the lie was even spoken, his brow would inadvertently furrow slightly, and he touched his nose once every four minutes, reaching a total of 26 touches during the testimony. Ultimately, the scientists concluded that several signs, including nose-touching, indicated that many of Clinton's statements were lies.

Touching the nose is a very common small action. Not only lying can prompt a person to touch their nose; other reasons may also cause it. For example, some people touch their nose simply because of pollen allergies, a cold, or discomfort from pressure by eyeglasses. Another example: when a person is in a state of unease, anxiety, or anger, the blood vessels in their nasal cavity also expand, and nose-touching may occur. Therefore, this is an auxiliary means to determine whether the other person is lying, not a definitive method.

When identifying whether someone is lying, other lying indicators must also be combined for interpretation. Because the purpose of touching the nose is self-soothing to relieve anxiety, and the source of anxiety does not necessarily come from lying. A simple example: in a noisy environment, some people are inherently prone to anxiety and will subconsciously rest their chin on their hand; the purpose is similar to touching the nose while speaking. Therefore, always remember this rule: simple nasal itching usually only triggers the single gesture of repeatedly rubbing the nose, with no connection to the content, frequency, or rhythm of the conversation; if some connection exists between them, you should be alert to the content of their speech.

#### Listening to the Nose's Voice

If there is a stranger around us, it is difficult for everyone to instantly judge them before they speak, because accent is an important basis for people to identify their compatriots. But accents can be learned and imitated; many actors are very good at speaking various dialects, yet people can still detect that this is a stranger. What is their basis? In fact, the nose plays a major role here.

When a person enters an unfamiliar environment, they can learn the local people's expressions, but they cannot fully relax their emotions as if among acquaintances. Nervous tension will still manifest in their body and expressions. In micro-expression changes, a person's discomfort with the environment can appear in the eyes, eyebrows, and corners of the mouth, but these parts are very easy to observe, so someone who deliberately wants to conceal themselves will block these signals. The nose, however, has never been noticed. Even if people in tense, unfamiliar environments have their accents corrected, they still cannot hide their nasal tone.

Nasal tone can be considered a very special signal among nose expressions. People who are conservative in thought and unwilling to break through themselves or change their current situation generally exhibit nasal tone. This is because they try hard to control their voice and nasal cavity; overly tense muscles make the area around the nose tight, the voice begins to be pushed backward, and nasal tone ultimately forms.

In addition to assisting the oral cavity in producing nasal sounds, the nose itself has its own way of vocal expression. Its unique structure gives the nose innate conditions for sound production. When stimulated by the outside world, the nose emits sounds in its own unique language, the most common being a sneeze.

Sneezing has physiological causes. Stimulation of the nasal mucosa from external sources or from a cold makes sneezing irresistible. Different irritating odors give sneezes many different meanings. Before sneezing, the nose shows frequent trembling accompanied by muscle twitching; a loud sneeze sends a clear signal: I don't like this smell! This can be considered the most passionate of all the nose's emotional expressions.

When people are in a state of sadness and begin to shed tears and cry, tears always attract maximum attention in an exaggerated way, and the wailing mouth is also an important component of crying, but the nose will also produce its own sound at such times. In a crying person, the nose emits a "sniff sniff" sound through constant twitching. The appearance of such a sound indicates that the person has received relatively strong stimulation and a high degree of emotional suppression; it serves as a judgment standard and signal for the level of grief. Sometimes, after the performance of tears and wailing ends, people may still remain in a state of sadness; at this time the nose will continue to emit twitching sounds to express its own inescapable low mood.

Sometimes the nose can reveal a person's true inner thoughts through sound. When a person expresses a skeptical attitude, the nose will be slightly raised, and at the same time a "tsk" sound will be emitted from the nasal cavity. Although they have not spoken, this sound is the clearest expression of their stance; the person producing this breath sound is clearly taking a negative attitude toward others' opinions.

#### III. Never Touch Your Nose When Lying

The nose has many forms of language. If you observe carefully, you can read from the nose's small movements many inner worlds that people deliberately try to hide. Among the many micro-expressions of the nose, the action of touching the nose must be mentioned. It is another characteristic of people when lying, in addition to facial or body language. If, when you ask someone a question, they hesitate and accompany it with a nose-touching action, you should consider whether they are concealing something about the matter you asked.

Long ago, Italian writer Carlo Collodi created *Pinocchio*. In the story, the young protagonist Pinocchio is a puppet; as soon as he lies, his nose grows longer. Although this is merely a fabricated fairy tale, it inadvertently illustrates that there is a certain connection between lying and the nose.

When people lie, many psychological reactions manifest physically. Some blush when lying, some dare not look the other person in the eye, and some involuntarily touch their nose. There are many examples in life. When football legend Pelé discussed his divorce again, out of a desire to conceal the truth, he involuntarily "stroked his nose" while answering reporters' questions to relieve his inner psychological burden. Former U.S. President Bush also made nose-touching movements when reviewing domestic affairs and answering reporters' questions about the Iraq War, prompting outside speculation about whether Bush's words concealed the actual situation. The act of touching the nose when lying is actually a manifestation of the "Pinocchio" effect.

The "Pinocchio" effect, simply put, is that during lying a person's nose enlarges due to increased blood flow; the instantaneous rise in blood pressure causes the nose to swell, which in turn causes nerve endings in the nasal cavity to transmit an itchy sensation. The person then lightly touches the nose with their hand to relieve the itch. This effect was summarized by scientists at the Smell & Taste Treatment and Research Foundation in Chicago through repeated clinical experiments. According to research results, when a person lies, a chemical substance called catecholamine is released, causing the cells inside the nasal cavity to swell. This proves that when lying, blood pressure rises and triggers a series of tiny bodily changes, including the nose-touching action.

The nose-touching action is very small and will not be noticed if one does not observe carefully, yet although the movement is small, it reveals your true inner situation and especially easily lets others know you are lying.

**Warm Reminder**: Touching the nose is a very common action, but not every instance of nose-touching absolutely means the other person is lying. Sometimes it may be because the other person has a cold or because the surrounding environment has caused nasal allergies, both of which can produce nose-touching actions. To determine whether the other person is lying while touching their nose, one must also combine context, speaking rhythm, and other body language for auxiliary identification.

#### The Nose's Expressions Are Ever-Changing

Observe the animals around you; many of them have flexible noses. A dog's nose is almost the most sensitive among all animals. Humans have used police dogs' noses to solve drug cases, allowing them to achieve repeated remarkable feats. Although the human nose does not possess such sensitive sensation, it is equally indispensable among micro-expressions. Whether expressing joy or conveying sadness, the nose has not fallen behind because of its structure.

When a person who has been busy all day returns home and smells the aroma of food, their joyful emotion is expressed not only through the eyes and mouth. When people are joyful, the nose performs noticeable expansion and contraction movements. Although the amplitude is not large, for a nose of this structure it already counts as a very passionate expression. This action frequently appears on people whose emotions are high; even without smelling the aroma of food, the nose's expansion and contraction will occur with similar amplitude. This manifestation of joyful emotion can also be conveyed through the slight flaring and gentle fluttering of the nostrils.

People often call arrogant individuals "looking at people through the nostrils." Although the nostrils do not possess the structure or function to look at people, during the emotional expression of arrogant people they very much like to play this role. A person who holds their head high conveys an attitude of disdain and pride; their raised-head appearance is exactly as if they are lifting their own nose high. In daily life, people who frequently hold their noses high are mostly aloof and unsociable individuals.

In addition to the various expressions it performs itself, the nose's expressions are also accompanied by coordination with other body parts: when frowning in displeasure, the nose also contracts along with the furrowed brows; when people smell an odor they dislike, they cover their nose with their hand. The action of covering the nose with the hand is a transmission of disgust emotion. Even without odor stimulation, people may still perform this action because they have seen someone they dislike or heard something they do not want to hear; this action has long become a way of transmitting unpleasant emotions.

Just as covering the nose with the hand is a covert transmission of unpleasant emotion, many of the nose's expressions are relatively covert. When communicating with others and wanting to understand their micro-expressions through the nose, one must have more patience and more meticulous observation.

#### The Nose That Stands Out Amid Calm

Although the nose occupies the geographically optimal central position on our face, many people have not paid attention to its expressions.

When you recall some impressive expression made by someone in your memory, you will find that the nose is always a part you cannot ignore. Even if you have not deliberately noticed it, it simply has this ability to become an important member of expression performance in the process of remaining obscure.

Among organs that transmit emotions, we often prefer to focus attention on the eyes and lips because these two parts are truly adept at expressing themselves. They are unrestrained and arrogant one by one, with exaggerated movements and the largest amplitude; their ever-changing modes of expression make it impossible for your eyes to leave them. Standing silently beside them is the nose. The human facial muscle structure gives the nose very little movement space; it does not have much exclusive expressive language. For this reason, the nervous system's distribution has also overlooked it and has not given it much "screen time."

But in reality, is the nose truly as bland and devoid of expressive desire as we think? You are wrong; it is the facial expression organ most likely to stand out amid calm.

Because the nose appears wooden in its performance, many people ignore it. Yet FBI researchers skilled in micro-expression studies have not let it slip away easily. They discovered that the human nose can almost be considered the most honest among all expression organs, because it is not good at disguising and is not easy to disguise; its reactions to external stimuli are always the most direct.

Although the nose's own structure appears insufficiently refined, the nasal cavity, as an important channel for communication between the human body and the outside world, is densely packed with many nerve endings. They can sense changes in the surrounding environment through breath and temperature, which are then manifested in the owner's facial movements. No one would think the nose also has a sensitive side; its muscle twitching and emotional expressions are most synchronized with the body's excitement and panic. At least from current scientific research results, the nose is very willing to participate in micro-expressions.

#### Pinching the Bridge of the Nose Is an Act of Deep Thought

If a person pinches the bridge of their nose with their hand, it often indicates that this person is focusing on and deeply considering the decision they are about to make. A person experiencing intense inner struggle will lower their head very low while pinching the bridge of their nose with their hand, as if to check whether they are truly in a predicament or whether this is merely a nightmare.

If we are asked a question that is difficult to answer, in order to conceal inner confusion and reluctantly produce an answer to cope, our hand will usually unconsciously move to the nose, touching it, pinching it, rubbing it, or even pressing and squeezing it with particular force, in a posture of "it's really difficult to ask me to answer."

When a person does this, it is best for us to remain quiet and wait for them to raise objections to the matter under discussion. We must make them understand that we acknowledge their feelings, will not apply any pressure to make them quickly emerge from thinking, and will patiently wait for them to voice their doubts<|eos|>

#### The Nose Also Reveals Hidden Intentions

**Micro-expression Keywords** The nose, as a respiratory organ, plays an important role in the human body. However, recently it has been discovered that different types of noses can reflect people's different personalities and hidden intentions. Some even say that if the shape of the nose changes, the personality will change accordingly.

Freud said in *The Aesthetics of the Human Body*: “A nose that is thin and pointed indicates a bad temper; a long and thin nose indicates a frivolous person; a person with a lion nose is easily deceived; a person with a hooked nose will never suffer a loss…” As soon as his remarks came out, people discussed them extensively. By the time of Aristotle, many began to believe that the nose is closely related to personality.

Modern psychologists have proven through research that different types of noses can reflect different personalities and hidden intentions. According to the clinical experience of a Japanese doctor: “Once a person undergoes rhinoplasty, those who were previously introverted often become stubborn individuals.”

#### One, The Nose and Temperament

Napoleon once said: “Give me a person whose nose should be large and full… Whenever I need to find someone to complete any useful mental work, if there is no other suitable candidate, I always choose someone with a long nose.” From Napoleon’s description, we can easily see that it is not without reason that people usually regard those with large and full noses as powerful or wealthy individuals. In addition, people believe that those with aquiline noses are very wise and intelligent, and also have a certain influence. The famous detective Sherlock Holmes is a typical representative of this.

As the saying goes, things resemble their owners. A person’s facial features can all reveal their personality traits. Just from the shape of the nose, one can roughly know a person’s temperament. So, what types are there approximately? The following is an analysis of different nose shapes and people’s temperaments.

#### Nose Wrinkling Indicates Disgust

A wrinkled nose usually indicates disgust (from mild dissatisfaction to extreme disgust), seemingly suggesting that the person has smelled a particularly bad odor.

Describing common behaviors indicating disgust as “turning up one’s nose” is most appropriate. This action clearly conveys a person’s dislike and opposition. Even infants instinctively turn their heads away from disliked food, as if avoiding the unpleasant smell, while adults tend to tilt their heads back.

Sometimes, a person’s wrinkled nose also indicates they are deep in thought and dissatisfied with one of their ideas.

#### Bag Nose

The nose is high, the bridge has a slight arc, the tip droops into a hook shape, and the wings are thick without exposed nostrils. Based on the shrewd and profitable character of Jewish merchants, this type of nose is also called a “Jewish nose.” People with this nose shape have a strong desire for money. For money, they can abandon everything—status, reputation, even human relations and morality—regardless of being reviled.

The nose sits at the center of the face, standing tall, connecting to the forehead above and the philtrum below. Its shape also clearly tells us what kind of personality its owner has.

#### Flared Nostrils Indicate Frustration or Anger

When a person’s nostrils flare, it indicates that a confrontation is about to occur. Psychologists generally believe that when people are frustrated or angry, their breathing becomes rapid and deep, and widened nostrils are the body’s way of taking in more oxygen, signaling preparation for a fight.

Animals behave similarly. A rancher in Texas once told us that an angry bull flares its nostrils and snorts loudly through them before charging. This is a serious warning that must be taken seriously.

#### Does Your Nose Attract Wealth

From the perspective of physiognomy, the nose is usually no less important than the eyebrows and eyes. The “wealth palace” refers to the nose, representing a person’s lifelong fortune and career. Having a “good nose” means having a “golden” future.

*The Complete Book of Divine Physiognomy* records: “The nose is the wealth star, residing in the earth mansion. If it is straight like a hanging tube or an ox gall bladder, it brings a thousand granaries and ten thousand chests. If it is upright and full, one will be wealthy throughout life. If it is centered and unbiased, one will enjoy continuous prosperity. An aquiline tip like a hawk’s beak brings financial loss and poverty.” We can observe a person’s nose to predict their wealth and temperament.

#### 6. Aquiline Nose

In many character illustrations, the figures have aquiline noses. Their noses resemble a hawk’s beak, with the tip drooping downward in a hook shape; the nostrils are barely visible from the front. Such people have quick minds, meticulous thinking, strong adaptability, and abundant energy. They can handle sudden and complex situations. The famous detective Sherlock Holmes and former British Prime Minister Tony Blair are representatives of the aquiline nose. People with aquiline noses are usually cold and cruel, and they prefer solitude. They constantly seek new sources of stimulation because they refuse to settle for the ordinary.

#### 10. Rounded Nose Tip

People with rounded nose tips are typical extroverted socialites. They are eloquent, kind to others, and possess sympathy and human warmth. They know how to maintain balance in relationships. Their optimistic and cheerful outlook helps them make many friends. If they leverage their diplomatic skills, they can achieve great success in their careers. However, such people tend to treat matters without proper priority and often start strong but finish weak. Their moods are unpredictable, with tempers that flare and fade quickly. In addition, their lack of wariness often leads them to be deceived.

#### 3. Greek Nose

Greek sculptures often feature noses with a straight, sloping bridge, so they are called “Greek noses.” People with Greek noses have high taste, excellent appreciation for beauty and noble arts, strong self-confidence, and lofty ideals. They are typical idealists who handle affairs methodically and earn widespread admiration. At the same time, they tend to be reserved in speech, and their natural arrogance can make others keep their distance.

#### 2. Long Nose

People with long noses have temperaments opposite to those with short noses. They are rational, possess strong self-esteem and a sense of responsibility, and do not allow others to tarnish their reputation or pursuits. They deliberate carefully and act cautiously, showing strong obsessive tendencies. Because they insist on considering everything thoroughly, they often overlook other matters, giving an impression of arrogance, and their social skills appear weaker. There is a folk saying that women with long noses usually marry well and live long lives.

#### Short and Low Nose

Such people have cheerful personalities, but their willpower is not very firm. They are relatively lazy and lack the courage to change their lives. If they fail at something, it is hard for them to recover. If they come from a poor background, they may muddle through life without achievement. They have few ideas of their own and are easily influenced by others, making them relatively easy to persuade. If female, they tend to lack ethical standards and are easily taken advantage of by men.

#### 1. Short Nose

People with relatively short noses are generally straightforward, simple, and honest, like children who cannot easily distinguish right from wrong. They often lack cunning and give others a relaxed, comfortable feeling. Such individuals are cheerful but lack deep consideration. When facing external temptations, they are easily swayed and may act impulsively. This trait is especially pronounced in women.

#### Straight Nose

This nose shape forms a straight line, neither too low nor very high, and appears comfortable to the eye. Such people have clear minds and generally enjoy smooth progress in work and career. They also have good luck with the opposite sex, though they are prone to being abandoned. At the same time, they tend to be overly concerned with minor details in everything they do, and they are somewhat selfish, thinking more of themselves than of others.

#### The Nose Enlarges When Lying

Did you know that your nose enlarges when you lie? The body’s reaction to lying is that extra blood flows to the face. Some people’s entire face turns red, and the nose may swell by a few millimeters. Of course, this swelling is invisible to the naked eye, but the liar feels discomfort in the nose and unconsciously touches it—this is a sign of lying.

#### 4. High and Straight Nose

Ancient texts describe an upright nose as an “isolated peak standing alone.” People with this nose shape are upright and full, confident, capable, and clear-headed. They achieve considerable success in their careers and can be considered outstanding individuals. However, they have high standards, like to haggle over small matters, and can be somewhat selfish. While capable themselves, they also hold others to strict standards.

#### 9. Pointed Nose

People with pointed noses generally have strong self-esteem and a self-centered tendency. Their speech is sharp and sarcastic. They can see into people’s hearts, and their cold exterior often gives an impression of being unapproachable. They resist criticism from others. Their withdrawn nature makes them dislike close interactions, yet this also gives them an advantage in being calculating.

#### People with Upturned Nostrils

People whose nostrils point upward let wealth come and go without accumulating it. Most such individuals are poor at saving money and spend wastefully without restraint. They usually only know how to spend money, not how to earn it, and they see nothing wrong with this. Ancient physiognomy texts say: “Nostrils pointing upward mean no grain stored overnight at home.” If such people become addicted to gambling, the consequences are disastrous.

#### People with a Flat Nose Bridge

A flat nose bridge makes it seem as if there is no nose at all. Such people are suited only to living honestly and accepting their fate. Because their financial luck is poor, they can only handle small amounts of money. Once they have more, it causes physical ailments or attracts others’ envy, leading to mental unrest. In addition, they trust others too easily, so money is often swindled away.

#### Long and Straight Nose

Such people are exceptionally talented, aesthetically gifted, and highly refined. They have deep appreciation for beauty and fashion and a strong understanding of art. They are idealists with a penchant for cleanliness, very confident in themselves, and sometimes arrogant. They also enjoy solitude and lack social skills, so they are not well-liked by those around them.

#### 5. Low Nose

A low nose is relatively short. Such people have temperaments opposite to those with high, straight or Greek noses. They tend to be content with the status quo, have few demands on themselves, lack confidence, and are somewhat lazy. They make no plans for life or work. Their frequent hesitation in making decisions causes them to miss many good opportunities.

#### Low Bridge and Pointed Tip

People with narrow noses, low bridges, pointed tips that are thin and sunken are inwardly malicious and often obtain wealth through fraud. One may refer to “Zhou Tiger’s” nose as an example. Such individuals usually have poor health, weak financial luck, and face frequent obstacles in their endeavors. Their marriages are prone to failure. If female, their husbands are certain to be unattractive.

#### 13. Rounded Tip with Full Wings

The nose symbolizes wealth. People whose noses have flesh are usually considered good at making money. Such individuals are upright and strict, responsible, positive, and willing to strive. They often excel in business. Their combination of investment skill and frugality means they need not worry about household finances.

#### The Nose Also Expresses Emotions

Generally, when interpreting others’ inner activities through facial expressions and features, one may not regard the nose as a highly expressive part because the information it conveys is far less rich than that from the eyes and mouth. Nevertheless, it has received attention from FBI agents, who have summarized the following three points of experience:

#### Straight Bridge with Rounded Tip

A straight bridge and a rounded, fleshy tip represent the perfect nose. Fleshy tips indicate a kind heart and good financial luck, with ample clothing, food, and shelter. Such people never deliberately pursue wealth, yet wealth comes to them.

In addition, those whose bridges curve left enjoy investing and want to gain without effort, while those whose bridges curve right are rather stingy.

#### 11. Small Nostrils

People with small nostrils handle matters like those with long noses: they deliberate carefully and act cautiously, living frugally. The novel’s miser Grandet is an example of this nose type. They are sensitive and anxious about gains and losses, making others reluctant to associate with them. They also lack foresight for the future.

#### The Nose: Mirror of Inner Activity

Is the nose only for smelling odors? If you think so, you are greatly mistaken. The nose can also leak secrets, but only if you are not paying attention. Although the nose generally does not move much, when combined with the other facial features it forms a whole that can expose a person’s inner secrets.

#### Aquiline Nose

The nose shape resembles a hawk’s beak, with the tip drooping downward in a hook. Such people often have sinister personalities and are cold and cruel. They are greedy by nature, insatiable in their pursuit of money and power, and lack human warmth. Although they may live long lives, their later years are lonely and desolate.

#### People with Lines on the Nose

Generally, people with horizontal lines on the nose are prone to hidden illnesses that are hard to treat; both marriage and career are likely to fail. People with vertical lines are prone to being adopted or to adopting others. If the vertical line is exactly on the tip, it is the “five horses dismembering the body” pattern; pay attention to traffic injuries.

#### Segmented Nose

The bridge has a segmented appearance in the middle. Such people are mostly stubborn and highly aggressive. In interpersonal relations they do not know how to compromise and never yield. They often offend others because of their personality and are not very popular.

#### 7. Depressed Nose

A depressed nose does not have a straight bridge; instead the bridge is collapsed and flat. Such people are relatively shy and lack sufficient self-confidence, yet they are cheerful and approachable, giving others a sense of inexplicable warmth.

#### 8. Broken Nose

A broken nose refers to a nose with a segmented appearance in the middle of the bridge. Such people are stubborn by nature, dislike others pointing out their faults, have quick tempers, and lack necessary coordination skills. Their unsociable behavior makes them prone to offending others.

#### Depressed Nose

A depressed nose means the bridge is not high enough—what is commonly called a flat nose. People with this nose shape are mostly cheerful and enjoy interacting with others, especially strangers, toward whom they have an inexplicable ability to feel close.

#### 12. Large Nostrils

People with large nostrils have temperaments opposite to those with small nostrils. They like to make many friends, have strong social skills, and do not fuss over trifles in life. However, they are careless in their actions and spend money like water, belonging to the “live for today” type.

#### People with a Low-Hanging Nose Tip

A nose whose nostrils are not exposed and whose tip hangs low indicates frugality and the ability to save money, even a tendency toward stinginess. Such people are good at calculation and financial management, making them suited to business and wealth accumulation. Those with wide, open wings can obtain unexpected or windfall gains.

#### People with an Crooked Nose Bridge

One can judge whether a person’s heart is upright by looking at the nose; a straight nose is very important. If the bridge is crooked, having money in hand will give rise to crooked thoughts.

#### How the Nose Expresses Emotions

##### How the Nose Expresses Emotions

When interpreting others’ inner activities through facial expressions and facial features, you may not regard the nose as an extremely emotionally expressive part, because the information it conveys is far less rich than that of the eyes and mouth. Yet it can indeed supply several body-language cues.

- **Flared nostrils indicate frustration or anger**: When a person’s nostrils flare, it signals that a confrontation is imminent. Psychologists generally hold that breathing becomes rapid and deep during frustration or anger, and the widening of the nostrils is the body’s way of drawing in more oxygen, foreshadowing preparation for conflict. Animals behave the same way. A Texas rancher once told us that an angry bull flares its nostrils and snorts loudly before charging. This is a serious warning that must be taken seriously.
- **Wrinkled nose indicates disgust**: A wrinkled nose usually signals disgust (ranging from mild displeasure to extreme revulsion), as though the person has detected an especially foul odor. The common expression “to turn up one’s nose” at something fits perfectly. The gesture clearly conveys dislike and opposition. Even infants instinctively turn their heads away from disliked food to avoid the unpleasant smell, while adults tend to tilt their heads backward.
- **Pinching the bridge of the nose is a sign of deep thought**: If someone pinches the bridge of the nose, it often means they are focusing on and weighing a decision. A person experiencing intense inner conflict lowers the head and pinches the bridge of the nose, as if checking whether the difficulty is real or merely a nightmare. Businesspeople frequently adopt this posture to show they are caught in a decision-making dilemma, conveying the sense that “answering is truly difficult.” When someone does this, it is best to remain silent and wait for them to raise objections to the matter under discussion. Let them know their feelings are understood, that no pressure will be applied to force a quick exit from reflection, and that their questions will be heard patiently. In most cases, pinching the bridge of the nose occurs together with closed eyes, a posture that represents strong internal doubt. In his book *The Art of Reading Minds: The White House Brain Trust*, “the father of negotiation” Gerard Nierenberg writes that a lawyer attending one of the seminars reported knowing a judge who habitually used this gesture to express thoughts and feelings about a case. If the judge believed the defendant guilty, the gesture did not appear; if the judge believed the defendant innocent, the gesture appeared, sometimes with the eyes closed for several minutes while the judge wrestled with how to rule.

Although nasal expressions are relatively few, the nose’s central position on the face still supplies clues to character traits, especially those a person tries to conceal.

##### Disgust

The common behavior that signals disgust is aptly described as “turning up one’s nose.” The gesture clearly conveys dislike and opposition. Even infants instinctively turn their heads away from disliked food to avoid the unpleasant smell. Adults tend to tilt their heads backward, an action often described as “looking down one’s nose” at someone.

The behavior of “turning away from someone” (or “cold-shouldering another”) likewise signals disgust at what a person says or does. In the deaf community, where visual experience is vital to communication, turning one’s back on someone who wishes to converse is considered the ultimate snub.

##### Reading Wealth from the Nose

In physiognomy the nose is usually considered as important as the eyebrows and eyes. The “wealth palace” refers to the nose and represents a person’s lifelong financial prospects and career. A “good nose” is said to indicate a “golden” future.

The *Complete Book of Spirit Physiognomy* records: “The nose is the wealth star and resides in the earth mansion. A nose shaped like a hanging gall bladder or a cut tube brings granaries and storehouses by the thousand. An upright, straight, and full nose brings lifelong prosperity and riches. A centered, unbiased nose ensures steady, abundant fortune. A nose with an eagle-beak tip (sharp and hooked) brings financial loss and poverty.” The following observations about the nose are offered for reference.

##### 7. Levator Labii Superioris Alaeque Nasi

The middle portion of the levator labii superioris alaeque nasi attaches to the major alar cartilage and the overlying skin; the lateral portion extends into the lateral upper lip (near the corner of the mouth) and merges there with the levator labii superioris and orbicularis oris. The muscle is bilaterally symmetrical.

Contraction of the levator labii superioris alaeque nasi has two effects: the middle portion widens the nostrils, while the lateral portion lifts and everts the upper lip, raising, deepening, and increasing the curvature of the top of the nasolabial fold.

##### People with a Low Nose Bridge and Pointed Nose Tip

A person whose nose is narrow, whose bridge is low, and whose tip is pointed, thin-fleshed, and sunken is considered inwardly treacherous and often obtains money through fraud. “Zhou the Tiger’s” nose may be consulted as an example. Such individuals usually have poor health, limited financial luck, and encounter repeated obstacles and difficulties in their affairs; marriage is also prone to failure. If the person is a woman, her husband is said to be unattractive or to lack the capacity to bring prosperity to his wife.

##### People with Upturned Nostrils

A person whose nostrils point upward lets money come and go without accumulation. Most such individuals find it hard to retain wealth, spend extravagantly, lack restraint, and understand only how to use money, not how to earn it; they themselves see nothing wrong with this. Ancient physiognomy texts state: “Nostrils pointing skyward, and the household has no grain left for the next night.” If such a person takes up gambling, the consequences are said to be disastrous.

##### People with a Flat Nose Bridge

A person whose nose bridge is flat, as though lacking a nose altogether, is advised to remain content with an honest, modest life and accept fate calmly. Because financial prospects are poor, such individuals can handle only small sums; once larger amounts appear, health problems or the envy of others arise, disturbing the mind. They also trust others too readily and are easily defrauded of money.

##### People with a Straight Nose Bridge and Rounded Nose Tip

A straight nose bridge and a rounded, fleshy tip constitute the perfect nose. Fleshy tissue at the tip is said to indicate a kind heart and good financial prospects, with clothing, food, and housing all abundant. Such people never deliberately chase wealth and status, yet wealth and status come to them.

In addition, a nose bridge that bends left indicates a fondness for investment and a desire for unearned gains, while a nose bridge that bends right indicates frugality bordering on stinginess.

##### People with Lines on the Nose

A horizontal line on the nose is generally said to indicate susceptibility to hidden ailments that are difficult to treat, with marriage and career both prone to failure. A vertical line suggests the person may be adopted or may adopt others; if the vertical line lies exactly on the tip, it is called the “five-horse dismemberment line,” and caution regarding traffic injuries is advised.

##### People with a Low-Hanging Nose Tip

A nose whose nostrils are not visible and whose tip hangs downward belongs to someone who is thrifty and able to save money, even to the point of miserliness. Such individuals excel at calculation and financial management and are suited to commerce. Wide, flaring nostrils are said to bring windfall or unexpected gains.

##### People with an Crooked Nose Bridge

Whether a person’s heart is upright can be judged from the nose. A straight, centered nose is considered essential; if the bridge is crooked, money in hand is said to give rise to dishonest thoughts.
