#### 2. Legs Apart

Spread legs display an open posture, a dominant signal, and an expression of absolute power, always conveying strength and authority. In this respect, humans and animals are remarkably similar: spread legs signify defense or resistance.

When two men meet and one perceives the other as weaker, he may spread his legs in a provocative gesture, asserting dominance. Spread legs can also signal preparation for attack.

When people sit down, they adopt different postures—crossing one leg over the other, keeping both legs together, crossing the ankles—and choose different positions, such as facing each other or sitting side by side. In fact, in interpersonal relationships, how one sits and where one sits both reflect deep psychological states. Therefore, we can mark and analyze a person’s sitting posture and chosen position to draw a “topographic map” of the heart.

#### (8) Dissolute Sitting Posture

Legs spread wide, hands with no fixed resting place, presenting an open posture.

Such people pursue novelty and can even set trends. Those accustomed to this posture usually smile readily and do not care about others’ criticism, so they enjoy good popularity. However, their living habits and thought patterns differ greatly from most people, easily leaving an impression of frivolity and sometimes causing family troubles.

#### People Who Cross Their Legs

This sitting posture appears natural and indicates that the person is relatively confident, knows how to handle complex interpersonal relationships, and knows how to enjoy life. However, if one leg hooks the other, it shows the person is cautious and reserved, lacks sufficient confidence, often hesitates when acting, and has a rather complex personality. Nevertheless, because they grasp the proper measure in dealing with others, they also win others’ liking and approval.

#### 1. Legs Together

The legs-together posture is serious, proper, and restrained; although it looks cautious, it can convey a sense of oppression and tension. Both the attention stance and sitting upright with knees together belong to this category.

Legs together is usually a submissive posture. For example, during military training every soldier is required to keep legs together. Therefore, when someone adopts this posture, it often represents submission.

#### Turned Feet

When a suspect feels relaxed about the conversation content, their feet usually point toward the agent. If the feet point elsewhere, something may be making them uneasy. For instance, when a suspect dislikes the agent they are speaking with, they will turn their feet toward the nearest exit. Although their upper body continues to listen attentively to the agent’s questions, their feet have already chosen to flee.

#### People Who Walk with Hands Clasped Behind Their Back Are Preoccupied

When a person is preoccupied, they usually walk slowly and often assume a contemplative posture—head slightly lowered, hands tightly clasped behind the back. They may occasionally stop to think, kick a stone, or pick up a piece of paper from the ground, as if saying to themselves, “Perhaps look at this matter from another angle.” Such people have usually encountered a difficult problem.

#### (1) Natural Standing

Legs naturally extended, neither tense nor slack, or slightly together.

People accustomed to standing naturally often lack pioneering spirit yet are down-to-earth, unwilling to compete with others, and relatively easy to satisfy. Emotionally they can be impatient and may pursue one person intensely for a period, yet they cannot withstand long-term tests. They do not know how to say “no,” so they get along well with others.

#### Legs Spread Apart

Legs spread wide is clearly a “territory defense” behavior. When a person feels pressure, agitation, or threat, they unconsciously spread their legs wider than others to emphasize their territory. For example, when two people in conversation enter a standoff, they typically spread their legs and feet. This is not to stand more steadily but to claim more territory.

#### Legs Spread Apart

Legs spread wide is clearly a “territory defense” behavior. When a person feels pressure, agitation, or threat, they unconsciously spread their legs wider than others to emphasize their territory. For example, when two people in conversation enter a standoff, they typically spread their legs and feet. This is not to stand more steadily but to claim more territory.

#### (4) Hurried Walking Posture

In non-emergency situations, if a person still walks hurriedly with long strides, it indicates abundant energy, emphasis on efficiency, no procrastination, and great integrity—they never shift blame—although they can sometimes be rash. In addition, if their footsteps are audible, fast yet orderly, it shows the person is rational, has a perfect plan for the future and life, and values relationships highly.

#### People Who Sit Upright and Still

Legs together, entire soles of the feet on the ground. Such people are sincere, open-hearted, and naturally warm. Although straightforward in character, they do not anger others. Their traits include orderly conduct, a tendency to be overly particular, and a pursuit of thorough perfection. They also avoid risky actions and lack sufficient flexibility, which can leave an impression of rigidity and formality.

#### Feet Together, Toes Lifted, Heels on the Ground

Such people are cautious, solitary, and withdrawn; they dare not blend into crowds and usually maintain a distant, defensive attitude toward others. This relates to their unusually sensitive nature—they cannot bear even slight criticism or discussion. Others sense this trait and therefore avoid discussing certain topics with them, which creates a sense of isolated loneliness and heightens their psychological defenses.

#### Legs Crossed

Usually we cross our legs when we feel comfortable and relaxed, but when someone we dislike suddenly appears we may immediately return to a normal posture. We also cross our legs when we feel confident in front of others. If one party crosses their legs during a conversation, it indicates that person is relaxed, and we can then discuss more important topics.

#### (5) People Who Like to Wear High Heels

High heels symbolize nobility and are favored by women who love beauty. It can be said that the thinner and higher the heel, the stronger the person’s desire to perform and attract attention. For the sake of beauty they are willing to endure some foot pain, so they actually possess considerable endurance. These women are either idle rich girls or accomplished career women.

Crossed legs is a defensive posture, generally indicating shyness, timidity, casualness, and lack of enthusiasm. For example, the leg-crossing posture when standing, or the crossed-legs posture when sitting. When speaking, if the body is upright with legs crossed and one leg raised, it indicates a skeptical mood. Additionally, when feeling uneasy or wanting to reject someone, people often make this rejecting gesture.

#### (1) Gentle Sitting Posture

The legs and heels are held tightly together, the hands rest on the knees, and the body is upright.

Such people are generally introverted, humble, with a closed emotional world; their speech and actions are relatively mild. For those with outgoing emotions, this can be hard to endure. #### Toes Together, Heels Apart

They possess strong insight and can accurately judge a stranger’s character at the fastest speed. However, they sometimes overestimate their own abilities.

#### Analysis of Sitting Posture Types

Such people appear amiable and approachable, yet are actually indifferent. They will not proactively help others unless sincerely asked. #### (1) Always Wearing One’s Preferred Style

#### Feet Shifting from Side-to-Side Rocking to Kicking

When a person’s foot movements shift from gentle side-to-side rocking to up-and-down kicking, it indicates that the person has seen or heard something negative or unpleasant. This is entirely an unconscious behavior; most people are unaware of it. Although these actions do not necessarily indicate deceptive intent, they do show that the current topic has affected the person.

#### People Who Walk with Chin Raised Are Arrogant

Some people walk with chin lifted, head held high, arms swinging exaggeratedly, striding forward with heavy, slow steps, as if deliberately trying to make an impression. #### Sleeping on One’s Back

Such people are very outgoing and generous, warm and kind, full of sympathy, willing to give, able to read others’ psychology well, and aware of others’ needs. Their thinking is quite mature; they can usually distinguish priorities in people and matters. They also have a strong sense of responsibility, dare to take on duties, and maintain relatively good interpersonal relationships.

#### One Leg Straight, the Other Bent or Crossed to the Side

This is a standing posture that conveys reservation or a slight tendency toward rejection. People accustomed to standing this way often lack confidence and are relatively shy; in an unfamiliar environment or among unfamiliar people they feel constrained. However, they are sincere toward others, inwardly warm, and enjoy helping people.

#### People Who Walk with Head Lowered Are Depressed

When a person is depressed, they often walk with head down, dragging their feet, hands in pockets, rarely looking up to notice where they are going.

One leg relatively straight, the other crossed in front or behind, heel slightly raised.

Leg-shaking in KTVs and restaurants is not done stealthily; it is done openly for pleasure and must be vigorous! But when the shaking is slight during conversation and was not present before, then this leg-shaking is the micro-reaction (微反应) flaw we are looking for.

#### Sitting with Legs Apart

Such people are open-hearted and may have a preference for taking charge of everything, possessing a leader’s temperament or a dominating personality. Such people have a strong defensive mentality and a strong sense of autonomy; they will not obey others’ orders or be manipulated, nor will they bow to power. They like doing what they enjoy; if someone forcibly requires them to do something else, they will resist.

People who stand without leaning to either side are often called “roly-polys.” That is to say, such people flatter and curry favor, are skilled at disguise. Therefore, they generally have deep scheming and can remain inscrutable.
