- The other party may have said something unfavorable to them, prompting them to accelerate their speech to express dissatisfaction and urgency.
- Another possibility is that they are reading a passionate battle manifesto or delivering an impassioned speech; the faster rate expresses strong inner emotion.

#### People Who Speak Rudely

#### Husky Voice

Women with a husky voice are usually very individualistic. Although they may appear delicate, their character is strong. They are courteous to everyone yet find it hard to reveal their true feelings, making them difficult to read. #### Situation-Forced Type

One day, A went to B’s home as a guest and arrived just as B’s family was eating. B politely invited him: “Have you eaten? If not, have some with us.” A had not eaten dinner, so he accepted without ceremony. The hostess, however, looked awkward because the noodles she had prepared were insufficient for another person.

A clearly failed to understand B’s true meaning. B had merely asked out of politeness and had no real intention of inviting him to eat. If B had truly wanted to invite him, he would have stood up to fetch bowls and chopsticks instead of merely moving his mouth. As the saying goes, “Listen to what is said and observe what is done.” When someone invites you, first watch what they do, or embarrassment may result.

#### Polite Remarks Still Need to Be Said

“Not everyone possesses the magnanimity to rejoice when told of their faults.” In real life, some people repeatedly claim they dislike polite remarks and prefer the truth. Yet if you truly act on that claim, they will certainly be displeased. Everyone likes to hear pleasant words and dislikes criticism. Polite remarks sound agreeable; even if exaggerated, the listener pays no mind and feels happy. If you omit them, others will find you difficult to get along with and gradually distance themselves.

Therefore, to maintain good social relations, one must say a moderate number of polite remarks. At the same time, one must discern the true intentions behind others’ polite remarks, cater to their preferences, and thereby win their favor.

#### 1. Fast Speakers

Fast speakers articulate as if firing a machine gun, finishing an entire thought in one breath with no room for interruption. Such people are generally extroverted, quick-thinking, eloquent, and adaptable. They are natural and generous toward others and see no need to hide anything, sometimes even recounting their own embarrassing moments without regard for image. They excel at socializing, handle interpersonal relations with ease, and achieve their goals effortlessly. Their strengths are lack of guile, inability to conceal anything, straightforwardness, and naturalness; their weaknesses are emotional volatility, impatience, decisiveness that borders on arbitrariness, and a tendency to act alone.

#### 3. Degree of Politeness

You may have noticed that the degree of politeness reveals changes in a person’s mood. Someone who speaks very politely feels favorably toward you and hopes to become your friend quickly; they are also straightforward and candid. If the two of you have already met many times yet the speaker remains equally polite, it indicates they wish only to maintain a working relationship or ordinary friendship. There are exceptions: some people, because of excessive vigilance, habitually keep themselves closed off or lack the ability to communicate deeply, and therefore remain polite. Such people are not truly being polite; they use politeness to keep distance.

#### 2. Gentle, Steady Tone

People with a gentle, steady tone are compassionate and helpful; they will not ignore those in difficulty, yet they act in a deliberate, unhurried manner. As conversation partners they may seem difficult at first, but they prove loyal and reliable.

Women with this tone are usually introverted; they control their emotions according to circumstances yet also long to express their views, so one should give them ample opportunity to do so. Men with a gentle, steady tone may sound honest at first, but they are actually rather stubborn; they hold firm to their opinions, rarely compromise, neither flatter others nor are easily influenced by others’ views.

#### Soft, Clinging Voice

Women whose speech carries a nasal, clinging quality are often vain and eager to be liked. Sometimes their excessive efforts to please backfire and cause annoyance. For children from single-parent families, this vocal quality indicates an inner desire for gentle treatment from elders.

Men who produce this sound are mostly only children or were pampered while growing up. They often feel lonely when alone and become confused or at a loss when required to make decisions. Toward women they are very reserved; when speaking with a woman alone, they appear especially nervous.

#### The Most Insincere Greeting—“How Are You?”

When they ask “How are you?” they are not genuinely concerned; they merely want to draw attention to themselves. Such people like to stand out, are full of self-confidence, yet frequently fall into deep thought. Before acting they like to deliberate repeatedly, then commit fully once they begin, with a determination not to stop until the goal is reached.

Everyone we meet has their own habitual greeting. The moment they open their mouth, their personality is exposed. In other words, we can judge a person’s character traits from their everyday greetings and thereby interact with them effectively.

#### 2. Moderate-Paced Speakers

People who speak at a moderate pace generally speak slowly but not so slowly as to cause impatience; they use a relaxed, gentle manner. A moderate pace is a relatively balanced speech rate. Such people are mostly gentle and kind, generous and benevolent, compassionate, and considerate. Their strengths are meticulous thinking, good planning ability, respect for others’ opinions while retaining their own distinctive views, and avoidance of blind conformity. Their weaknesses are conservative thinking, lack of mental agility, hesitation in action, insufficient self-confidence, lower acceptance of new things, and in extreme cases outright rejection, making success difficult.

#### Seeing Through the Other Person's Psychology from Their Way of Speaking

Everyone has a unique conversational style, and each style is in fact an expression of emotion. Preferences for topics, the manner of answering questions, the degree of politeness, and the way of refuting questions all reveal one's psychology.

When we communicate with others, we hope the conversation flows pleasantly and creates a sense of instant rapport. Yet the conversation does not always proceed as smoothly as we wish; various unexpected changes often arise. Therefore, we must learn to see through the other person's psychology from their conversational style, promptly detect emotions in their words that hinder the exchange, and then resolve them.

#### Section 2: Careful, Your Voice Reveals Your Secrets

The *Lüshi Chunqiu* states: “Hear the voice and know the demeanor; observe the demeanor and know the aspirations; examine the aspirations and know the virtue.” This means that listening to someone speak reveals their bearing, observing their bearing clarifies their interests, and understanding their interests discloses their moral character. Through the voice one can “hear the sound, know the person, and recognize the heart,” gaining a general sense of an individual's character or moral quality. Clearly, the voice readily exposes a person's secrets.

What aspects of the voice convey information? Primarily volume, tone, and pitch.

#### People Who Like to Discuss Matters in the Office

The office is a single-purpose venue where no one else will interrupt or affect the content and atmosphere of the conversation. Choosing this location indicates that such people generally approach others and situations with sincerity and are trustworthy. Moreover, they are confident in their work and regard it as the center of life; if they suddenly stop working one day, they become irritable and insecure. Generally, these individuals are highly responsible and conscientious, especially when handling matters entrusted by friends—they will spare no effort to complete them well. Consequently, they enjoy good popularity and earn the respect and trust of friends.

#### Acquaintances Exchanging Polite Remarks

Generally, when we are very familiar with someone, we do not exchange many polite remarks, as doing so would seem distant. If a very familiar person suddenly becomes overly courteous, it may indicate dissatisfaction and a deliberate attempt to distance themselves. At such times, one should reflect on one's own words and actions or any impropriety that offended the other party and repair the relationship promptly. In the case of romantic partners, it is quite possible that the other person has done something wrong and feels guilty, hence offering many polite remarks to please you; we should then pay attention or find ways to uncover the truth.

#### The Habit of Answering Questions Reveals Character Secrets

Micro-expression keywords The process of conversing with others is interactive and always involves questions and answers. The way one answers questions can inadvertently reveal character secrets. Therefore, discerning personality from the other person's answers and adjusting one's speaking style in time can enhance communication effectiveness.

When conversing, we inevitably ask others questions or answer their questions. From the habit of answering, one can discern a person's character secrets. Generally, answers fall into the following personality types:

#### People Who Like to Discuss Matters in Open Spaces

For example, squares or rooftops—places where one need not worry about eavesdroppers causing trouble. Such people are broad-minded, optimistic, and straightforward, yet they also have a timid side. Most are men. They harbor grand ambitions, pursue long-term goals, and act steadily. At the same time, they are skilled at concealing their true feelings; once someone enters their inner world, they cherish that person greatly.

With this understanding, if someone invites you to discuss matters at a particular location, you can first learn about their character and approach to life and prepare accordingly.

#### The Most Common Greeting — Hello!

This is the word used most frequently and in the widest range of situations when meeting others. Whether addressing a stranger or an old friend, whether in public or in the office, greeting with “Hello!” is always the safest choice.

People accustomed to this greeting tend to have calm minds, control their emotions well, and dislike making a fuss. Whatever they do, they are diligent and meticulous, earning the trust of colleagues and friends. They treat others honestly, say what they mean, rarely engage in direct conflict, and enjoy good popularity.

#### People Who Speak in a Pedantic Manner

This type of person usually has a strong educational background and likes to use ornate language, introducing large amounts of irrelevant information during conversation. In life they affect an elegant style; outwardly confident, they are inwardly insecure. They also enjoy showing off their knowledge. As the saying goes, what a person flaunts is precisely what they lack. Outwardly well-mannered, such individuals actually lack self-assurance and therefore assume an air of superiority in conversation. They are empty inside—an ornamental facade.

#### People Who Like to Expose Others' Privacy

When four or five people gather, the conversation often revolves around someone's private matters. Some expose others' privacy; naturally, others listen. This is an interesting subject. I have studied the psychology of such people and found that they enjoy revealing others' secrets either out of hostility, envy, inferiority, or jealousy. When with them, one must be very cautious, because if they disclose someone else's privacy to you, they will just as readily disclose yours to others.

#### The Choice of Venue for Discussions Reflects One's Approach to Life

Daily social interactions require a venue—restaurants, bars, offices, homes, and so on. The choice of location when discussing matters reveals a person's approach to life. Whether they are smooth or rigid, honest or cunning, can be discerned to some degree.

When people need to discuss something, some invite others to a restaurant for a meal, others choose the office, and still others prefer a bar. Different venues highlight different approaches to life.

#### One's Personality Can Be Seen from Greeting Words

Micro-expression keywords Greeting others upon meeting is common courtesy, and everyone has their own greeting style and habitual phrases. These are closely tied to personality. In other words, we can read a person's character from the way they greet and thereby pave the way for future interactions.

Personality traits manifest in the small details of daily life. Greeting is the most ordinary daily occurrence. What character does each greeting style reveal? Let us examine them together.

#### People Who Like to Say "Absolutely"

Psychological research shows that people who frequently use the word “absolutely” tend to be subjective, self-centered, and inclined toward self-love. They also employ “absolutely” as a defensive excuse or shield when proven wrong—for example, “I will absolutely never do it again” or “I will absolutely never act that way again.” Such assurances initially inspire trust, but over time they make the speaker appear inconsistent in word and deed.

#### (III) People Who Deliberately Step Back and Maintain a Certain Distance from You

Greeting is meant to foster closeness, so encountering such people can feel uncomfortable. At first I assumed they were inwardly closed off and socially inept, but after several encounters I discovered they actually maintain fixed social circles; once that familiar circle is breached, they experience panic and rejection. Understanding this, you know what to do: when interacting with them, keep a certain distance so they feel safe.

#### People Who Show an Expression of Disbelief

Some people react to praise with great surprise as a way of reciprocating the compliment. These individuals are undoubtedly endearing; they are honest and simple, often suffering losses while helping others. They enjoy group activities and treat others generously, thus maintaining good interpersonal networks and remaining popular in both life and work. Because they are overly generous toward others, they sometimes endure grievances and may even implicate family or friends.

#### Glib-Tongued People

This type is calculating and shrewd. They have usually seen a bit of the world and are driven by self-interest. They are generous toward themselves yet extremely stingy toward others. Their character is unstable; they are smooth and worldly-wise, thoroughly versed in the rules of social interaction. Such people are hypocritical and adept at concealing their true thoughts. One may associate with them but should not become close.

#### People Who Seem to Know Everything

Some individuals possess broad knowledge, understand a little about many subjects, cite widely, and appear profound. Yet their minds are cluttered with unsystematic information; when facing a difficult problem they often miss the point. They may offer several suggestions, none of which hits the mark. If they consciously strengthen their analytical ability and grasp the essence of matters, they may well become well-rounded talents.

#### High-Pitched and Sharp Voices

Women with high-pitched, sharp voices tend to have fluctuating emotions, clear likes and dislikes, and may easily contradict their past statements without realizing it. Such people are also prone to sentimentality or sudden anger over minor matters.

Men with high-pitched, sharp voices are fervent by nature, easily excited yet also easily fatigued. A characteristic of these individuals is that they master the art of success by leveraging their personality at a young age.

#### Those Who Pretend to Understand When Answering Questions

These people are face-conscious and highly vain. They dread being mocked for ignorance, so they pretend to understand. They are also stubborn, unwilling to accept others' opinions, and will argue heatedly with anyone who disagrees, refusing to yield until the other party concedes. If they are in the right, they press their advantage relentlessly. Consequently, within groups they are generally kept at a respectful distance.

#### Fullness

Whether the other person's voice is rich or thin, firm and powerful or light and gentle, serves as an important reference for judging their personality. Generally, a full, varied voice is perceived as strong and trustworthy.

In short, the voice contains many subtle elements. Grasping their micro-changes allows us to understand others while consciously imitating and adjusting to establish consistency.

#### Those Who Avoid the Real Issue When Answering Questions

These people are smooth operators who seek advantage and avoid harm. Generally, when faced with unfavorable situations they try to muddle through. They also employ unorthodox methods, letting others do the work while they reap the benefits. In addition, they are timid, unwilling to take responsibility, and quick to shift blame for fear of becoming involved in any trouble. They are poor at seizing opportunities; even good ones slip away while they hesitate.

#### (I) People Who Look Directly at the Other Person

Such individuals possess strong self-awareness. In conversation their words are often probing and aggressive. Becoming close friends with them requires time and effort, because they are inwardly guarded. My approach with them is to respond with a gentle gaze and relaxed tone. You must neither be intimidated by their stare nor confront it directly, or the conversation will stall.

#### People Who Like to Discuss Matters in a Tea Art Gallery

Tea art galleries offer a degree of privacy and allow one to conceal one's true identity—underground agents in television dramas, for example, often meet there. Such people are extremely cautious in their dealings, handle everything carefully, and rarely reveal their intentions. They usually present a relaxed façade to extract information or gain trust from others. They belong to the highly calculating type.

#### Those Who Are Flashy but Substance-Lacking When Answering Questions

These individuals are eloquent and articulate. When answering questions they speak volubly and at length. At first hearing they give the impression of being knowledgeable and expressive. Upon closer scrutiny, however, their answers sound impressive yet miss the point entirely. Such people tend to be seasoned, hypocritical, and cunning. When dealing with them, be careful not to be deceived by their fine words.

#### People Who Like to Discuss Matters at Home

Choosing home indicates familiarity with the environment and no concern that unexpected people or sounds will disturb the conversation. This suggests that such individuals are relatively weak-willed, timid, and poorly adapted to the outside world. In work and life they often suppress themselves, conceal their emotions, and keep joy or anger from showing. Consequently they frequently feel pressure without knowing how to release it, becoming increasingly exhausted.

#### People Who Like to Discuss Matters in Restaurants

Restaurants are public places filled with people and chatter. Choosing such a venue first indicates that these individuals are bold and unafraid of their privacy being overheard; second, they are ambitious and confident that they can avoid or solve any problem. Moreover, they are exceptionally intelligent and can devise various methods to handle sudden difficulties.

#### (II) People Who Often Go Off-Topic

These individuals have an intense desire for control and self-expression.

Conversing with them often leaves one confused, because they constantly digress, shift topics, and speak at length. If you cannot endure their pace, here are two simple, effective tactics:

1. Deliberately drop an object to interrupt them
2. Immediately leave the scene—that is, disappear from their sight

#### People with Intense Speech

These individuals possess rich knowledge, speak sharply and rapidly, and offer profound, original insights into human affairs, often hitting the mark directly. They adapt quickly to new things and react swiftly, yet they feel at a loss when confronted with matters beyond their ability. Once they seize an opponent's weakness they launch a fierce counterattack, sometimes becoming so obsessive that they trap themselves in a dead end.

#### The Shyest Greeting Method — Hi!

Such people are shy and sentimental. They act with extreme caution, fearing criticism for mistakes, and therefore dare not undertake innovative or pioneering endeavors. In social interactions they are usually taciturn and unwilling to go out with friends, preferring to stay home with their partner. However, with familiar people they display warmth and enthusiasm, deliberately trying to please.

#### Calm and Composed People

These individuals are courteous and steady. They express gratitude appropriately to those who praise them. They maintain independent principles, advance steadily toward their goals, excel at keeping a low profile, avoid ostentation and arrogance, and work pragmatically and single-mindedly. If you have such a subordinate, pay close attention—they may well bring you substantial returns and become your right-hand person.

#### Those Who Pretend to Be Erudite When Answering Questions

These people possess some talent and are not entirely ignorant of various subjects, yet they know only the surface and speak in generalities. In personality they are somewhat clever yet rely on that cleverness and refuse to study diligently. Their interests are broad, but lacking perseverance they cannot master any subject deeply. At work they lack a sense of responsibility, cannot handle specific tasks competently, and certainly cannot lead.

#### Those Who Parrot When Answering Questions

These individuals lack independent views or original thought. When required to answer a question they merely repeat others' words without offering their own opinions. They are vain, appropriate others' theories for display without citing sources, and possess strong imitative ability—anything they hear or see they can basically reproduce. Employers can certainly make use of this trait for their own purposes.

#### Chapter 8: Hearing the Voice, Distinguishing the Person, Knowing the Heart

A person's words are the simplest and most direct way to convey inner thoughts. Different psychological reactions often manifest through different words and expressions. Language and micro-expressions are closely linked, and micro-language is a true reflection of one's inner world. Therefore, through a person's voice we can discern their character and then infer their thoughts.

#### People Who Praise Each Other

Those who immediately return a compliment with a corresponding remark generally possess independent personalities. They dislike relying on others and are full of self-confidence. In interactions they place great value on equality, so you need not worry about suffering losses nor expect to gain advantages from them. Such people carry presence in the workplace and enjoy challenges.

#### 1. Slow Down Your Speech Rate and Adjust Your Mood

When angry, try regulating your breathing until it becomes even and silently remind yourself: “Stay relaxed; you must remain calm.” If your emotions are still agitated, close your eyes, think of things that make you happy, and attempt to view yourself from the other person's perspective. This will naturally calm you down.

#### People Who Like to Discuss Matters in Bars or Clubs

Choosing such venues satisfies many of the other party's desires while providing a legitimate pretext. It also elevates their status, expands their influence, and aids goal achievement. In reality, these individuals are often fame-seekers who act ostentatiously and love to show off. They pursue success yet frequently fail because of some personal desire.

#### People Who Like to Use Humor to Mock Others

Most of them have a narrow mind and strong jealousy. They sometimes even do things that go against their conscience or kick someone when they are down. In addition, they have a strong sense of inferiority, a negative attitude toward life, and often negate what they themselves have done. Being picky and sarcastic toward others is their specialty. They spend all day plotting how to scheme against others, yet they themselves have never truly been happy.

#### Identifying People by Their Voices, Delving into Their Hearts Through Sound

The strength, speed, pitch, and clarity of a voice can also reveal a person’s complex inner emotions. Not only can voices help us observe and understand people, but even the instruments they play can reflect the player’s psychological state.

The following sections explain how to discern a person’s character and psychology from their voice.

#### People Who Speak Quickly and Directly

This type of person usually has a forthright character, acts with integrity, and possesses a very open heart. Their inner thoughts align closely with their words and actions. They tend to trust their own feelings, say whatever is on their mind, and keep nothing hidden. Because of their direct and candid nature, they cannot keep secrets about their own affairs or those of others. As a result, their moods shift rapidly and they show little persistence in what they do.

#### People Who Nod or Shake Their Head Repeatedly

People who nod repeatedly during conversation appear to understand and agree with the other person’s views, yet they tend to act rashly. Often they make promises they cannot keep, leaving others with a poor impression. What about those who shake their head repeatedly? Clearly they are arrogant and self-willed; winning their approval is extremely difficult.

#### People Who Stare at the Other Person

This type of person has a strong desire for control and will seize any opportunity to display themselves. They do as they please, dislike being constrained, yet possess enough intelligence and presence to accomplish tasks others cannot. Once they set a goal, they pursue it relentlessly. Their unrestrained personality, however, sometimes leads to misunderstandings.

#### How a Person Accepts Praise

Praise affirms achievement and is something most people desire as an external response. Receiving praise often brings inner satisfaction and pleasure.

Dangerous situations test courage, the ability to handle trivial matters reveals patience, and the manner in which a person accepts praise likewise reflects their true character and emotions.

#### Self-Control

From childhood, parents and teachers teach us to restrain ourselves. “Be patient” is one of the phrases we hear most often. We also use similar words to overcome depression, anxiety, and other emotions, the most important of which is suppressing anger. As we grow older, we gradually learn to mask our feelings and regulate our behavior through various postures.

#### The Most Enthusiastic Greeting Style—“I’m so glad to see you!”

This type of person is outgoing, warm, and modest. They enjoy participating in all kinds of activities and easily blend into new groups. They are helpful; when friends need assistance, they never stand idly by, regardless of whether they can actually help, and thus win good relationships. Their drawbacks are a tendency to fantasize, a lack of rationality, and being easily swayed by their own emotions.

#### People Who Like to Say “Whatever”

When ordering in a restaurant and asking what the other person wants to eat, one often hears the word “whatever.” If the two people meet only occasionally, this may be politeness. For someone already familiar who still frequently says “whatever,” the person is usually easygoing but also indicates a lack of personal opinion in daily life.

#### People Who Like to Be Different

This type can be divided into two kinds. One kind is highly curious, dares to say “no” to authority, and possesses a spirit of challenge and exploration; however, they can be extreme and lack calm thinking. The other kind habitually uses language to cover up inferiority, showing off literary flair and spouting new theories that sound impressive but are merely rehashing old ideas.

#### Catchphrases Reveal a Person’s True Nature

In daily life, many people unconsciously use certain words or phrases repeatedly while speaking; these are called “catchphrases.” As the saying goes, “habit becomes second nature,” and to some extent these linguistic habits best reflect the speaker’s real psychology and personality. The following sections introduce some of the most common catchphrases.

#### Taciturn People

Most people of this type are either overly self-conscious or excessively calculating. They usually do not want to reveal their inner thoughts, so others cannot know the real them. They have a strong sense of self-protection and can often focus on their own careers. They show good persistence, can persevere, and maintain a stable character without major fluctuations.

#### People Who Like to Create Prank-like Humor

Most are lively, outgoing, warm, and generous. They live relatively lightly; even under pressure they find ways to relieve it. They dislike restraint, are rather mischievous, and enjoy joking with others. In the process they entertain themselves and also hope to share that joy with others.

#### The Most Gossipy Greeting Style—“Any fresh news?”

This type of person usually has an extremely strong curiosity and wants to get to the bottom of everything. Some even pry into others’ private affairs and gossip behind their backs, which makes them unpopular. At the same time, they are keen on material comforts and pursue them relentlessly. Their advantage is that they plan thoroughly before acting and proceed in an orderly manner.

#### A Rough, Deep Voice

People whose voices are rough and deep—whether male or female—enjoy doing good deeds and hope to be leaders. They are active types who dislike staying quietly at home. Both men and women with this voice have wide circles of friends and can associate with all kinds of people. Women with such a voice tend to have good relationships and are trusted by others.

#### Subtle Changes in Voice

Voice is a powerful tool for building rapport. Skilled salespeople, negotiators, and speakers know how to adjust their voices to align with others and gain favor. Therefore, you must first identify the other person’s vocal characteristics before you can move closer to matching them.

#### Reading Minds Through Speaking Gestures

A person with full use of their limbs can hardly speak without accompanying gestures. Some gestures are habitual; others are made to emphasize tone or content. Whether intentional or not, these movements allow us to glimpse certain “psychological codes.”

#### Volume

Voice carries power, and the strength of that power reflects a person’s inner traits. For example, if the other person speaks softly while you prefer to speak loudly, reaching agreement will be difficult. Likewise, to gain the approval of loud-voiced people, you should raise your own volume.

#### People Who Use Humor to Break an Impasse

They possess strong adaptability. Most have a strong desire to perform and hope their actions receive attention and recognition. Their outstanding performance may make them the center of attention, which satisfies their need for self-expression.

#### The Most Straightforward Greeting Style—“Hey!”

People who open with this greeting are relatively frank and direct. They are energetic, lively, and cheerful. They tend to be optimistic and open-minded when facing difficulties. They also think quickly, possess a sense of humor, are flexible in dealing with others, and can accept opposing opinions.

#### People Who Become Shy When Praised

Some people blush the moment they receive praise and appear bashful. They are generally fragile and sensitive; criticism hurts them, let alone sudden setbacks. Yet they are compassionate and do not use words to hurt or attack others.

#### (7) People Who Strongly Deny

They are modest and dislike being disturbed, so they spend much time maintaining their independent space. Humor and boldness are only their outward appearance; in reality they deliberately close themselves off, making it difficult to form deep friendships with others.

#### Abnormal Voice and Tone

A liar’s voice may unconsciously rise because they are trying to conceal inner unease. Therefore, if the other person’s voice suddenly rises during a conversation, it is time to be on guard.

#### People Who Like to Say “I’m only telling you”

“I’m only telling you,” yet in fact they tell everyone. Most people have this habit. Those who frequently say “I’m only telling you” are rather ridiculous and display immaturity; such people are not suited to keeping secrets.

#### People Skilled at Self-deprecating Humor

They have a broad mind, readily accept others’ opinions and suggestions, and often engage in self-reflection and self-criticism, seeking out and correcting their own mistakes. They enjoy good interpersonal relationships.

#### People Who Like to Spread Rumors

This type is a typical prankster. They talk nonsense and delight in stirring up trouble, yet their intentions are not truly malicious. Their purpose is simply to attract attention and satisfy their vanity.

#### Chapter 4: The Profound Meaning in Words—Deciphering the Mysteries Behind What Is Said

“A fool who keeps silent leaves even a sage at a loss.” Once the other person opens their mouth, it becomes easy to grasp their character traits, perceive their inner activities, understand their knowledge and cultivation, and judge their living conditions.

#### (3) People Who Speak with Flattery and Artful Words

Some people frequently use sweet talk and flattery to achieve their goals or gain business advantages. Soft-hearted individuals often fall into their traps, so one must remain vigilant.

#### (6) Absent-minded People

They are mentally agile, exceptionally intelligent, and talented. They are both realistic and decisive, do not pursue fame and fortune excessively, and do not care overly about others’ praise. Self-confidence and boldness are their most obvious character traits.

#### Seeing Through an Opponent via Conversation Style

A person’s conversation style largely reflects their true nature. Therefore, mastering the connection between conversation style and personality makes it easy to see through someone’s inner thoughts.

#### People Who Constantly Touch or Scratch Their Hair

Most of this type are thoughtful, highly motivated, and detest evil. They belong to the active group. When they touch or scratch their hair, they are usually thinking and observing.

#### (5) Unmoved People

They are conscientious and low-key at work, disliking attention because they feel it would distract them. They are not competitive and let things take their natural course.

#### People Who Like to Say “I”

People who frequently say “I” possess a childlike or feminine character and a strong desire for self-display. Those who often use the plural form are usually lacking in individuality, submerged in the collective, and inclined to echo others.

#### Both Speed and Tone Reveal the Heart

A person’s emotions and opinions are clearly expressed in their words. With careful attention, even the meanings between the lines gradually become apparent beneath the curtain of speech.

#### People Who Like to Say “I know”

When the other person repeatedly says “I know” during conversation, it means they no longer wish to listen. At that point it is best to end the conversation or change the topic.

#### The Most Direct Greeting Style—“Come here!”

This type of person tends to act decisively, enjoys taking risks, and can learn from failures. They are also willing to share their feelings and experiences with others and like to express themselves.

#### (1) People Who Stick Strictly to the Matter at Hand

This type usually has clear goals, acts decisively, and behaves with integrity, though they sometimes give an impression of rigidity. A large portion of them experience interpersonal difficulties.

#### (2) People Who Do Not Look at the Other Person

This type often lacks self-confidence. Even before meeting, they have already anticipated every possible difficulty, so deep down they are unwilling to interact with strangers.

#### People Who Prepare Humorous Remarks in Advance to Show Their Sense of Humor

Most prefer formal things and place great importance on how others view them. Their attitude toward life is serious and restrained.

#### A Gentle, Steady Voice

This type of person is generous and kind-hearted, yet not quick or decisive in response. They belong to the careful, long-considering type and prefer to uphold tradition and hold conservative views.

#### People Who Like to Say “So”

The most striking trait of people who frequently say “so” is their tendency to regard themselves as clever and self-righteous.

#### (4) People Who Do Not Respond

Such people are undoubtedly arrogant; they believe your greeting is an attempt to curry favor and therefore refuse to acknowledge you.

#### People Who Like to Say “I can’t…”

On the surface this type appears modest, but in reality they are quite incompetent.

#### Speaking Speed

##### Speaking Speed Reveals Inner Changes

Speaking speed can reflect a person's emotions while speaking. Therefore, by listening to someone's speaking speed, we can determine their emotional state.

When people speak, they are engaging in an exchange of ideas as well as a natural expression of their psychology and emotions. Many people know only that the content of speech directly conveys the speaker's thoughts, yet they overlook how other factors can also reveal the speaker's psychology and emotions. For example, the pace of a speaker's delivery directly indicates their personality and psychological state.

1. **Extremely Fast Speaking Speed**  
   If someone speaks at an extremely fast pace, like a machine gun firing without pause, the listener can easily miss important information if they are not careful. This indicates that the speaker has an extroverted personality, strong self-awareness, and likes to control the conversation, dominating the exchange. The speaker's rapid pace stems from keen interest in the topic and eagerness to express themselves, along with concern about omitting thoughts that have just occurred to them. In addition, when the speaker has something to hide, intends to lie, or feels inner tension, their speaking speed will involuntarily quicken in an attempt to conceal their true thoughts.

2. **Extremely Slow Speaking Speed**  
   If someone speaks at an extremely slow pace and stammers, it suggests a weak, introverted personality marked by low self-esteem and reluctance to interact with others. People who speak very slowly are often mild-mannered, though they may sometimes be sensitive and prone to depressive moods. However, slow speech does not always indicate weakness, introversion, or low self-esteem; it can also reflect a calm, steady personality. Such individuals think while speaking, maintain stable emotions, avoid impulsiveness, and remain composed in any situation.

3. **A Normally Fast Speaker Suddenly Slows Down**  
   If someone who usually speaks quickly suddenly slows their pace, it shows they consider what they are about to say very important and want others to hear and remember it clearly. For instance, when a leader reaches a key point during a meeting, they will instinctively slow down so subordinates can follow without missing the main points. Yet a sudden slowdown by a fast speaker is not always meant to draw attention; it can also serve to convey emotion and resonate with listeners. During a speech, for example, the speaker may deliberately slow down to express certain feelings. In addition, when a speaker feels sad or distressed, their mood grows heavy and their normally rapid pace slows. If someone who is usually eloquent suddenly becomes slow and hesitant, the reason is obvious: they are hiding something or have done something wrong, leaving them lacking in confidence, nervous, and uneasy.

4. **A Normally Slow Speaker Suddenly Speeds Up**  
   If someone who usually speaks slowly suddenly accelerates, they may be trying to mask inner unease. For example, when a lie is exposed, the person often rushes to explain, becoming incoherent and using an extremely fast pace to conceal their discomfort. A sudden acceleration by a slow speaker can also result from emotional agitation; excitement, anger, fear, impatience, anxiety, or tension can all cause an abrupt increase in speed.

##### Psychology Mini-Class

Security Bureau psychological experts note that a person's speaking speed and tone can reveal their inner world. This is why we can sense whether the other party is in a good mood during a phone call even without seeing them.

When Security Bureau agents interview a subject, two or three officers typically participate: one converses with the subject, another observes body language, and a third focuses on the subject's speaking speed and tone. This arrangement underscores how closely changes in tone, speed, and pitch relate to the inner world. Indeed, solving cases through speaking speed has become a secret technique that helps Security Bureau agents accelerate investigations.

Security Bureau psychological experts have found through research that speaking speed is the primary feature for analyzing how a person speaks. Fast speakers are often eloquent, while slow speakers tend to be more taciturn. In psychology, however, the key is to understand the other person's psychology by noting deviations from their usual manner of speaking.

Security Bureau agents solve cases through speaking speed not because they possess supernatural powers or mind-reading abilities, but because speaking speed directly reflects psychological state and emotional fluctuations, allowing insight into a person's thoughts.

In daily life, we can also accurately grasp a person's rich psychological changes by observing shifts in their speaking speed and pitch, and even, based on these external changes, acc

##### Speaking Speed Suddenly Slows

When a person feels weighed down—for instance, when sad or confused—their speaking speed also becomes very slow. During news broadcasts, whenever a disaster or the death of an important figure is reported, the announcer deliberately slows down; the principle is the same.

In addition, when people harbor dissatisfaction or hostility toward someone, their speaking speed slows and may even take on a somewhat wooden quality. Although they try not to display their discontent or hostility, the more they attempt to conceal it, the more obvious it becomes.

In short, speaking speed can subtly reflect a person's psychological state while speaking. Paying close attention to others' speaking speed and its variations ensures that their subtle inner activities will not escape your notice.

##### People Who Speak Slowly

Such individuals are generally unhurried by nature. They not only speak at a measured pace but also remain calm even when facing urgent matters. They are kind-hearted, generous, compassionate, and considerate of others. Women of this type tend to be gentle. Generally, these people maintain inner calm, think carefully and methodically, enjoy planning, listen to others' opinions, and yet retain their own distinctive views. Because they are approachable and speak tactfully, they enjoy good interpersonal relationships. Their drawbacks include conservative thinking, resistance to new ideas, rigid adherence to principles, slightly slow thinking, hesitation in action, and lack of decisiveness.

##### People Who Speak Quickly

These individuals speak like a string of firecrackers—rapidly and without allowing others to interrupt. They are generally intelligent, think quickly, and possess strong adaptability, which contributes to their fast speech. Most are extroverted, articulate, and skilled at tailoring their words to the listener. They excel in social settings, win others' favor, and readily achieve their goals. Their shortcomings include an inability to keep matters to themselves, occasionally revealing things better left unsaid. They also tend to be short-tempered, easily angered by minor issues, and prone to arbitrary decisions that may lead them to act willfully.

##### Different Speaking Speeds Reflect Different Inner States

When people speak, they exchange ideas and simultaneously reveal their emotions. Variations in speaking speed indicate different inner conditions. For example, if someone who is normally eloquent suddenly stammers, or if someone who is usually taciturn suddenly becomes talkative, there must be a reason: their psychology has undergone a fundamental shift. Therefore, carefully observing a person's speaking speed and its changes allows one to grasp their psychological state.

##### Speaking Speed Suddenly Accelerates

Research indicates that people suddenly speed up when they are nervous, angry, excited, impatient, or fearful. They hope rapid speech will relieve their inner agitation. Because they have not thought calmly, however, the content of their speech often becomes empty. Anyone who is cautious and perceptive can immediately detect their wavering inner state.

##### Speaking Speed

If your speaking speed is too fast, the other person's thinking may not keep up, impeding communication. If it is too slow, the listener may grow bored and wish to end the conversation early. Therefore, maintaining a pace the other person can accept is very important; the simplest method is to mirror their speaking speed.

##### People Who Speak Extremely Slowly

These individuals speak very slowly, often hesitating and rambling. They have overly weak, introverted personalities, lack confidence, appear dull, and act sluggishly.

#### Pitch and Intonation

##### Changes in Speaking Voice Can Reflect Inner Changes

Micro-expression keywords: Generally speaking, a person’s voice remains steady while speaking. However, when special circumstances arise and subtle inner changes occur, the voice will shift accordingly. Therefore, variations in a person’s voice not only reveal emotional shifts but also expose inner activity.

During the Spring and Autumn period, Zichan, prime minister of the state of Zheng, once went out on an inspection tour. He saw a woman weeping at a grave and ordered her arrest. His attendants were puzzled. Zichan explained, “Although her crying is loud, there is no grief in it—only fear. There must be something false here.” Later interrogation confirmed that the woman had been having an affair and had plotted to murder her husband.

From a person’s voice one can discern not only emotion but also inner changes.

**Speaking in a very loud voice**  
Such people are straightforward and open, treat others sincerely, and speak directly without beating around the bush. They often offend others unintentionally. Although they recognize this trait, they will never change their manner of speaking. In addition, they are upright in character, act openly and honorably, and command respect. They also possess good organizational skills and a strong sense of responsibility, earning others’ trust. They are therefore well suited to leadership roles.

**Speaking in a very soft voice**  
Such people lack confidence and breadth of mind. They often quarrel with others over trivial matters. They are usually deep and calculating, skilled at scheming, and determined to succeed at any cost—even by unscrupulous means. In dealing with others they are snobbish and never reveal genuine feelings. Consequently, although they may achieve career success, they have few close friends.

**Voice suddenly rising from low to high**  
Three psychological reasons generally account for this:

1. Strong emotional agitation. When stimulated, a person loses emotional control and the voice rises involuntarily. For example, someone who suddenly wins a prize will excitedly shout “I won!” to share the joy; likewise, during an argument with a loved one, anger is hard to suppress and the voice grows louder.
2. Attempting to persuade the other party. In a debate, when a speaker becomes excited, the words are almost shouted in order to make the listener accept the opinion. In moments of urgency, people subconsciously hope the volume will intimidate the other side; raising the voice also boosts the speaker’s own confidence.
3. Wishing to dominate or command the other party. This is common when parents address children, teachers address students, or superiors address subordinates. Raising the voice reinforces authority and elicits obedience.

**Voice suddenly falling from high to low**  
Two reasons explain this:

- One is running out of arguments and losing confidence. When confident, a person speaks with full volume; when sensing a weak position, the voice gradually drops. For instance, a child who has erred may still argue while being scolded by a parent, yet the voice grows softer as the questioning continues.
- The other is inner fear and unease. When confidence gives way to anxiety, the voice also descends. For example, an employee reporting to a silent boss may worry that something was done poorly and will speak more and more softly.

Voice changes are thus inseparable from the speaker’s current psychological state. Differences in volume, weight, pace, and length correspond to differences in inner activity. The saying “hear the voice, know the person” captures this principle.

##### Speaking Tone Can Also Reveal Personality

Micro-expression keywords: Voice does express character. When facial expressions, gestures, or words fail to reveal a person’s mindset, try reading tone to gauge personality and emotion.

In daily life some people speak softly and gently, others heavily and authoritatively, and still others in a high, clear tone. As the saying goes, “Listen to the tone when hearing words; water the roots when watering a tree.” Different tones reflect different personalities. No one forgets the character Little Swallow played by Zhao Wei in the television drama *My Fair Princess*; wherever she goes, her loud voice is audible, perfectly matching her carefree and impulsive nature.

##### People Whose Voices Are High and Sharp

Such individuals tend to be neurotic, sensitive to their surroundings, creative and imaginative, and possessed of excellent aesthetic sense. They are also assertive: in social interactions they point out others’ faults without mercy, regardless of embarrassment caused. As a result they are often disliked. At the same time they possess strong insight and original thinking, quickly identifying the essence of any issue. When this trait is fully utilized, success comes more readily.

##### People Whose Voices Are Soft and Gentle

Such people are usually mild-tempered, indifferent to fame and fortune, and rarely become entangled in conflicts of interest. They get along easily with others and maintain good relations. From another angle, they are timid and avoid involvement in disputes, adopting an evasive stance. With guidance and encouragement, however, they can enter competition, display their talents fully, and become balanced individuals capable of both firmness and flexibility—people destined for significant achievement.

##### People Whose Tone Is Mild and Steady

Such individuals often display an elder’s composure. They consider matters thoroughly, act methodically and unhurriedly, and possess strong endurance; once a goal is set, they persevere steadily. Men of this type can be somewhat stubborn, holding to their own views and neither swayed by others nor inclined to flatter. They may be difficult at first but prove loyal and reliable. Women of this type are compassionate, understanding, and willing to make sacrifices for others.

##### People Whose Voices Are Affectedly Sweet

Such people speak in a coquettish manner in hopes of winning affection and protection. Yet they are restless and prone to fabricating lies, which ultimately repels others. When male, they are often only children raised with excessive indulgence. Such men tend to be indecisive, uncertain when judging situations. Toward women they are very reserved: one-on-one conversations make them extremely nervous, and they never take the initiative.

##### Intonation

Does the other person maintain a single intonation throughout? When finished speaking, do they use a falling or rising tone? These are points to observe. Some people show little intonation change, making their true intent hard to discern; others vary intonation richly, rendering their words easier to understand. Judge character from intonation, then adjust your own tone to accommodate the other person.

##### Pitch

Cultural influences on behavior lead us to use pitch to emphasize gender. Generally, when seeking attention, men tend to produce a muffled, low sound from the throat while women produce a sharp, light sound. At such moments, pause or lower your voice to show respect.

##### People Whose Tone Is Strong and Resolute

Such individuals are open-minded, distinguish right from wrong clearly, act honorably, uphold principles, and maintain strong organizational discipline. However, they lack flexibility, can be rigid, and rarely allow room for discussion, which may offend some. Because they remain impartial and realistic, they gain the support of most people.

##### People Whose Tone Is Tactful and Mild

Such people are broad-minded, cheerful, generous, benevolent, sincere, and possessed of sympathy and tolerance. In social dealings they navigate situations skillfully and rarely incur blame. They are not quick to accept new things yet do not oppose them, generally maintaining an understanding attitude.
